pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup.explain: sim_bringup is the 'start button' of the simulator: its launch file sim.launch.py starts Gazebo, spawns the drone, starts ArduCopter SITL, MAVProxy, the SIYI camera emulator, the payload release node, the ROS-Gazebo bridge, RViz and the demo panel in the right order. It also holds the small command-line helpers the shell scripts in simulation/scripts use: mission_tool (upload, arm, start over MAVLink), phase_monitor (prints the mission phases), stack_check (waits until the team code is ready), photo_trigger (one photo), wait_then_exec, gz_follow and odom_tf. sim_paths.py is the one place that answers every 'which file / which port' question.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup.how_it_fits: It sits between the operator's scripts (demo.sh, start_sim.sh, fly_mission.sh) and every other simulator package: it reads world configs from sim_worlds, builds the drone file from sim_models, starts siyi_emulator and sim_demo, and has MAVProxy share SITL's MAVLink on UDP 14550 (scripts / ground station), 14552 (the old MAVROS door, now only a fallback) and 14553 (demo panel), plus a copy for Mission Planner on Windows. The team's MAVROS connects straight to SITL SERIAL2 (TCP 5763+10I, the FCU_URL demo.sh and start_sim.sh pass), wired like the real Jetson on the Pixhawk's TELEM2. team_stack.launch.py runs the team's unchanged tracker.launch.xml with only the detector model path pointed at a file that exists on the laptop; the team code itself is never changed by this package.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.explain: The tests of sim_bringup: pytest unit tests that need no simulator (mission file reader, phase state machine, sim_paths, wait_then_exec, the SIYI packet builder, the launch argument list and the Gazebo window layouts in config/), run_tests.sh (pytest + launch files parse + shellcheck of the simulator scripts + every --help) and the developer tool gen_rviz_window_state.py.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.how_it_fits: Run with 'python3 -m pytest -q test' or 'bash test/run_tests.sh' from the package folder; nothing here runs in a simulation.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models.explain: sim_models is the simulated DRONE: the Gazebo model iris_a8mini (ArduPilot's Iris quadcopter + a SIYI A8 mini 3-axis gimbal with a live video camera and a triggered photo camera + two droppable payloads), the extra ArduCopter SITL parameter file astra_sitl.parm, the payload_release node that drops a payload when ArduPilot opens servo 11 or 13, and the generate_model_sdf tool that turns the xacro source into a plain SDF.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models.how_it_fits: sim_bringup's sim.launch.py runs model.sdf.xacro through xacro and spawns it as entity 'iris'. In Gazebo the model's ArduPilotPlugin talks to ArduCopter SITL over the JSON physics link (UDP 9002+10I, lock-step): SITL outputs 1-4 spin the motors and outputs 11/13 are copied to the Gazebo topics /sim/payload/servo11 and /servo13. The siyi_emulator moves the gimbal (/sim/gimbal/*/cmd_pos) and triggers photos (/sim/camera/photo/trigger); the ROS bridge carries /sim/camera/*, /sim/drone/odometry and /sim/gimbal/joint_states to ROS; payload_release turns the team's DO_SET_SERVO 1400 us into a visible drop; sim_demo's scoring reads where the payloads landed.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.explain: The tests of the simulated drone: pytest unit tests (release and landing logic, the SITL parameter file read the way ArduPilot reads it, model generation for both camera profiles, the payload_release node with a fake Gazebo, the camera geometry) and the heavy flight acceptance test in acceptance/ with its own test world in worlds/.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.how_it_fits: Unit tests run with colcon test or 'python3 -m pytest -q test --ignore=test/acceptance'; the acceptance test (run_acceptance.sh) starts headless Gazebo + SITL and is run by hand.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds.explain: sim_worlds holds the PLACES the simulated drone flies over: the Gazebo worlds 'runway' (a small fast test field near the real SUAS site) and 'suas_field' (the SUAS 2026 field at Skyway Range, Oklahoma), each with its config file (world file, SITL home, spawn pose, mission, truth), its search mission in the exact shape the team code expects, and a truth file saying where the hiker (mannequin) and tent really are. It also holds the generators that build those files (scripts/build_*.py with the worldgen helpers), small Python libraries (geo, survey, mission, planner, world_config, truth, gzrun) and checking tools; the realfield sub-package and data/ are the work-in-progress real-terrain world 'suas_field_real'.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds.how_it_fits: Files only, no running node: sim_bringup's sim_paths reads config/<world>.yaml to start Gazebo with worlds/<world>.sdf and to give ArduCopter SITL the matching --home; demo.sh uploads missions/<world>_survey.waypoints through mission_tool; sim_demo (truth_detector, demo_markers, score_run) reads truth/<world>.yaml to fake detections, draw markers and score the run. The hook adds share/sim_worlds/models to GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH so Gazebo finds model://sim_worlds_*.

Needs numpy and Pillow, only to RE-GENERATE worlds.

Reads --seed, --assets, --altitude (must be inside the SUAS band 45.7-121.9 m), --textures and --out-dir, writes the shared models, builds the field (and creek model), writes the world, config, truth and both missions, and prints a summary.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: Proves a world is healthy, headless, in about 30 seconds: it loads the world in its own partition with temporary GPS probes at the origin and on every target, runs about 12 simulated seconds, and checks that the log has no [Err] lines, the contract systems (Physics, UserCommands, SceneBroadcaster, Sensors, Imu, NavSat) loaded, the real-time factor, that the config home equals the world's spherical coordinates, and that every probe reports its expected WGS84 position within 0.5 m. Prints PASS/FAIL (exit 0/1) and can write JSON.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: Run by test_sim_worlds.sh and by hand after changing a world (ros2 run sim_worlds check_world.py runway).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Reads latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation and heading_deg from a world's text and returns them as a geo.Home, or None when latitude or longitude is missing.
Finds one <name>number</name> tag in the world text and returns the number, or None.
Horizontal distance in metres between two nearby GPS points, using a flat local approximation (111,132.95 m per degree north, 111,412.84 x cos(latitude) per degree east).

Loads the world (by name via world_config, or an .sdf path) and its truth file, injects NavSat probes, starts HeadlessGazebo (verbosity 4), subscribes with gz-transport to each probe and to /world/<name>/stats, waits until the simulated time and all readings are in (or the 180 s timeout), then evaluates errors, systems, real-time factor, home and GPS, prints a report and optionally writes JSON.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.effects: starts and stops its own headless gz sim; writes a log under /tmp/sim_worlds_check

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Makes a callback for one GPS probe that stores its latitude, longitude and altitude under that probe's name.
Stores one NavSat reading (latitude, longitude, altitude) of the probe, under a lock.
Records the real-time factor and the current simulation time from each world statistics message.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: Downloads, ahead of time, the 17 Gazebo Fuel models the worlds use (Rescue Randy lying and sitting, four people, three vehicles, oak and pine trees, cone, barrel, drum, chair, table, tent) at their pinned versions into Gazebo's Fuel cache (~/.gz/fuel or $GZ_FUEL_CACHE_PATH), skipping cached ones and retrying 3 times. '--check' only reports what is missing (exit 1 if any), '--list' prints the URLs.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: 03_build.sh runs it once (~110 MB) so the first world start does not freeze while downloading; the list must match worldgen/assets.py (a unit test checks).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Turns an 'owner/name/version' entry into its Fuel download URL https://fuel.gazebosim.org/1.0/<owner>/models/<name>/<version>.
Turns a model entry into its folder in the local Fuel cache: <cache>/fuel.gazebosim.org/<owner lowercase>/models/<name lowercase>/<version>.
Succeeds when the model's cache folder already holds a model.config or model.sdf, i.e. the model is downloaded.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: Downloads (or copies with --from) every raw input of the real-terrain world into ~/.astra_sim/world_data/suas_field_real/raw/ and proves each file with a checksum from data/real_field_manifest.json. Methods: http (file SHA-256), cog_window (reads only a pixel window of a big cloud GeoTIFF such as the NAIP photo, checks the pixel SHA-256), overpass (OpenStreetMap at a fixed date, checks sorted elements), ms_buildings (Microsoft footprints of one quadkey, keeps those in the box) and copy_only. Planetary Computer files need a free anonymous token fetched on the fly.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: Called through fetch_real_field_data.sh; only needed to re-generate the WIP real-terrain world (stage 1 input).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Finds real_field_manifest.json in the source tree, an install layout or the installed share folder; exits with a message if it is nowhere.
SHA-256 fingerprint of a file, read in 1 MB pieces.
SHA-256 of the decoded pixel values of a GeoTIFF (all bands), so the check does not depend on the GDAL version that wrote the file.
SHA-256 of an Overpass JSON's elements sorted by (type, id) as compact JSON, ignoring the header (which carries a time stamp).

Checks a downloaded file with the checksum kind of its method (pixel, elements, features or file SHA-256) and returns whether it matches the manifest (a missing expected value counts as OK), the measured value and the kind.
SHA-256 of a GeoJSON file's features, each as sorted compact JSON, sorted and joined by newlines.
Downloads a URL to a .part file and renames it into place (so a broken download never looks finished), retrying up to 3 times with growing pauses.
Adds a Microsoft Planetary Computer access token for 'account/container' to a file URL, fetching and caching the free anonymous token from the Planetary Computer API the first time.

Reads a big pixel window of a remote cloud GeoTIFF in 1024 x 1024 pieces, retrying each failed piece up to 4 times with a fresh token, so one dropped connection does not throw away a 183 MB read. Returns the pixel array and the source's profile adjusted to the window.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.inputs: URL, token account, bands, window column/row/width/height

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Reads the manifest's pixel window of one or more cloud GeoTIFF bands and saves them as one compressed, tiled GeoTIFF (band order = the URL or band list order).
Sends the manifest's OpenStreetMap Overpass query (it carries a fixed date) to each endpoint until one answers valid JSON, and saves the answer.

Downloads the dated Microsoft building-footprint file of one quadkey (unless a verified copy is there), keeps the buildings whose centre is inside the box, writes them as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection and deletes the big download.
Looks for a manifest file inside a --from folder: the same relative path, else the same file name (or an alias) anywhere below.

Reads the options (--data, --from, --only, --optional, --check, --force, --record, --list), loads the manifest, and for every chosen source verifies an existing file or copies / downloads / window-reads / queries it and verifies the result; --record writes measured checksums back into the manifest (maintainers). Prints a summary; exit 1 if any file is missing or wrong.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.called_when: fetch_real_field_data.sh (which runs it with an isolated Python that has rasterio)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.effects: downloads into ~/.astra_sim/world_data/suas_field_real/raw; may rewrite the manifest

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: Wrapper that picks a Python with the GIS libraries (GIS_PY, else ~/.astra_sim/gis_venv/bin/python, else python3; warns when rasterio is missing) and runs fetch_real_field_data.py with -I (isolated, so files in the download folders can never be imported). '--setup-venv' creates ~/.astra_sim/gis_venv with rasterio, pyproj, laspy, scipy, numpy, Pillow and PyYAML. Required layers are about 400 MB.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: Only for re-generating the WIP real-terrain world; flying the normal worlds needs nothing from it.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: (Re)makes or checks a world's search mission. It reads the search area and survey settings from config/<world>.yaml, plans the lawn-mower lanes for the 2560x1440 / 81 deg camera, writes the QGC WPL 110 file and prints it as a table with the team indices and a shape check. Options change altitude, overlaps, photo interval, speed, lead-in, area and output; '--check FILE' only prints and checks an existing file. Exit 1 when the shape check finds problems.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: The recipe for changing a simulator mission (AGENTS.md 'Change the mission'); test_sim_worlds.sh runs its --check on both missions.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Reads a mission file, prints it as a table (mission.describe), prints the team indices (takeoff, DigiCamCtrl, buffer_wp where photos stop, hold point, RTL, where targets are inserted) and the shape check, and returns the list of problems.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.inputs: path, optional altitude band, optional Home

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: With --check it only checks the given file. Otherwise it loads the world config, picks the search area (default the survey area), builds SurveySettings from the config plus the command-line overrides, plans the mission, writes it (default the config's mission path), prints a summary line and checks the written file at exactly the planned altitude.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: Takes still pictures of a Gazebo world from cameras you place yourself, with no drone and no window: it adds static preview cameras to a temporary copy of the world (each publishes /preview/<name>/image), runs a headless server in its own partition, waits --settle simulated seconds so textures load, saves one PNG per camera and stops its own server. Default camera: 2560x1440 with the A8 mini's 81 deg lens; pose form NAME:x,y,z,roll,pitch,yaw or look-at form NAME:x,y,z@tx,ty,tz.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: A developer tool for checking how the hiker, tent and grass look from the drone's height and for making detector test pictures.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Reads one --camera text into name, position, roll/pitch/yaw, width, height and field of view; the look-at form computes pitch and yaw from the camera towards the target point. Bad names or numbers raise ValueError.
Writes the SDF of one static preview-camera model (preview_cam_<name>) with a camera sensor of the given size and field of view publishing on /preview/<name>/image at 2 Hz.
Turns a gz.msgs.Image (8-bit RGB or BGR) into a numpy picture array in RGB order; None when the data is incomplete.

Parses the cameras, injects them into the world text, starts HeadlessGazebo, subscribes to each camera and to the world statistics, waits until every camera saved one frame (or the timeout, reporting progress every 15 s), and prints where each PNG was saved and the median real-time factor.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.called_when: ros2 run sim_worlds render_preview.py --world FILE --out DIR --camera ...
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.effects: starts its own headless gz sim; writes PNG files and gz_server.log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Makes the image callback for one preview camera.
Saves the first frame of this camera that arrives after the settle time as <name>.png and records when.
Records the real-time factor and simulation time from each world statistics message.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: Runs every check of sim_worlds in one go with PASS/FAIL per step: 1 the pytest unit tests, 2 both mission files checked with make_mission.py --check, 3 the Fuel cache (warning only), 4 a headless load of each world with check_world.py (skipped with --quick or without the gz command). Exit code = number of failed checks.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: Installed tool: ros2 run sim_worlds test_sim_worlds.sh [--quick].

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Prints a blank line and '=== <step title>' to start a new check.
Prints '--> PASS: <name>' when the given exit code is 0, otherwise '--> FAIL: <name>' and counts the failure.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.explain: Prints facts about a world from its config/<world>.yaml so shell scripts never hard-code paths or coordinates: '--list' prints the world names, 'world_info.py runway' prints everything as YAML with absolute paths, and 'world_info.py runway home' prints one field (world_file, world_name, home, spawn, spawn_x/y/z/yaw, mission, truth, share, models).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sc.how_it_fits: A command-line tool (ros2 run sim_worlds world_info.py ...) built on sim_worlds.world_config; the README uses it to open a world with gz sim.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.explain: Returns the printable value of one field of a loaded WorldConfig (home as the SITL text, spawn as 'x y z yaw', models = <share>/models); an unknown field raises KeyError.
Reads the arguments, then prints the list of worlds, one field, or the whole config as YAML. Unknown worlds or fields print an error and return 2.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/scr.outputs: exit code 0 / 2; the answer on standard output

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Marks sim_worlds as a Python package and lists its light helpers (geo, survey, mission, world_config, truth; only PyYAML needed). The worldgen sub-package (numpy + Pillow) is only needed to re-generate worlds.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Lets other packages write 'from sim_worlds import geo'.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Converts between GPS latitude/longitude and the local metres Gazebo uses (x east, y north, z up, origin = the pad centre = home), plus small polygon helpers. It has TWO conventions: 'ardupilot' (default) copies ArduPilot's own sphere formulas (Location::offset / get_distance_NE), which SITL uses to make the drone's GPS, so photo names, MAVROS positions and waypoints all match it; 'wgs84' is the exact ellipsoid a Gazebo NavSat sensor reports. Inside the worlds they differ by at most about 1 m.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by mission/planner (waypoints), truth (scoring), the world generators, check_world.py and the realfield code. sim_demo does not import it: it has its own geo.py for the same ArduPilot convention.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The world origin as a GPS position: lat, lon (degrees), alt (metres above sea level of the ground at the origin) and heading (degrees, 0 = north). The same four numbers go into SITL's --home and the world's <spherical_coordinates>.
Reads a 'lat,lon,alt_msl[,heading]' text (the SITL --home format, heading optional = 0) into a Home; wrong count or out-of-range latitude/longitude raises ValueError.
Writes the Home as SITL's --home text with 7 decimals for latitude/longitude and 1 for altitude, e.g. '36.2143000,-96.0068000,210.0,0'.
ArduPilot's longitude scale: the cosine of the latitude, never below 0.01 (how much shorter a degree of longitude is than a degree of latitude there).
Moves a GPS point by some metres north and east exactly like ArduPilot's Location::offset (sphere of radius 6378100 m, longitude scaled at the mid latitude).
Metres north and east from point 1 to point 2, exactly like ArduPilot's Location::get_distance_NE (longitude difference wrapped to -180..180).
Turns WGS84 latitude, longitude and height into Earth-centred X, Y, Z metres.
Turns Earth-centred X, Y, Z back into WGS84 latitude, longitude and height with 8 refinement steps (about 1 mm exact).
Returns the east, north and up directions (as Earth-centred unit vectors) at a GPS point, used to turn local metres into Earth-centred offsets and back.
Local metres (x east, y north, z up) from home -> exact WGS84 latitude, longitude and altitude, the way a Gazebo NavSat sensor reports it.
Exact WGS84 latitude, longitude, altitude -> local metres east, north, up from home.

Local metres (x east, y north) -> latitude/longitude. Default convention 'ardupilot' (what the drone's GPS reads above that spot); 'wgs84' gives what a NavSat sensor reads; anything else raises ValueError.
Latitude/longitude -> local metres (x east, y north), the inverse of enu_to_latlon, in either convention.
Compass heading (degrees, 0 = north, clockwise) -> Gazebo yaw (radians, 0 = east, counter-clockwise): yaw = 90 deg - heading.
Gazebo yaw (radians) -> compass heading in degrees between 0 and 360.
True when the point (x, y) is inside the polygon, using the even-odd ray-casting rule (count how many edges a ray to the right crosses).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: x, y, list of (x, y) corners

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The shortest distance in metres from a point to the outline of a polygon (closest point on any edge).
True when the point is inside the polygon AND at least 'margin' metres from its outline (used to keep objects away from boundary edges).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Starts and stops a HEADLESS Gazebo server safely for tests and tools, in its own GZ_PARTITION and process group (so it never disturbs a running demo, and stop() never kills other Gazebos), and adds temporary helper models (GPS probes, cameras) to a copy of a world.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by check_world.py (load test, real-time factor, GPS check) and render_preview.py (pictures).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns the name in <world name="..."> of a world text, or None.
Returns the world text with extra SDF snippets (models) inserted just before the last </world>; raises ValueError when there is no </world>.
Writes the SDF of a static 'GPS probe': a model check_navsat_<name> at (x, y, z) with a NavSat sensor publishing on /check/<name>/navsat at 5 Hz.
Builds a GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH that finds this package's models (the models/ folder next to the world's worlds/ folder), plus extra folders and whatever is already set.

A headless 'gz sim -s -r' server on a (possibly modified) copy of a world, with a unique partition name worlds_<pid>_<time>, its own log file and safe stop; usable with 'with HeadlessGazebo(...) as gz:'.

Stores the world path and text (read from the file if not given), finds the world name, makes a unique partition and a log path, and remembers verbosity, extra resource paths, whether to keep the temporary world and an optional iteration limit.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: world path, optional text, log path, verbosity, extra paths, keep_world, iterations

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The environment the server and our own gz subscribers must share: GZ_PARTITION = this partition, GZ_IP 127.0.0.1 (unless set) and the resource path.

Writes the world text to a temporary .sdf, copies the partition settings into this process (so its gz-transport nodes join), starts 'gz sim -s -r -v N [--iterations K] <tmp world>' in a new session with output to the log, and turns Ctrl+C / SIGTERM into an exception.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.effects: starts a gz sim server process; writes a temporary world and a log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Signal handler that raises KeyboardInterrupt, so a Ctrl+C or 'timeout' still reaches the code that stops the server.
True while the server process is still running.
Stops OUR server only: SIGTERM to its process group, SIGKILL if it does not end within 15 s; closes the log, deletes the temporary world (unless keep_world) and restores the old signal handlers.
Starts the server when a 'with' block begins and returns it.
Stops the server when the 'with' block ends, even after an error (the error is not swallowed).
Returns everything the server printed so far with the colour codes removed ('' if the log cannot be read).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Reads and writes ArduPilot mission files in the QGC WPL 110 text format (what Mission Planner and MAVProxy 'wp load' use), builds the search mission in EXACTLY the shape last year's flight code expects (0 home, 1 TAKEOFF, 2 first lane waypoint, 3 DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL, optional DO_CHANGE_SPEED, lane ends, R-2 = last lane end where photos stop, R-1 = hold point, R = RETURN_TO_LAUNCH) and checks a mission against that shape.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by planner.py, make_mission.py and the world generators; team_indices copies the index logic of waypoint_manager and main_controller so a mission can be checked without running them.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: One line of a QGC WPL 110 file = one MAVLink mission item: seq, current, frame (0 absolute, 3 above home), command number, param1-param4, x/y/z (latitude, longitude, altitude for NAV items) and autocontinue.
Readable command name, e.g. 'NAV_WAYPOINT' or 'DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL' ('CMD_<n>' if unknown).
True for the NAV commands main_controller counts as physical items (command numbers 16 to 22).
Writes the item as one tab-separated line formatted like Mission Planner writes it (8 decimals for parameters and lat/lon, 6 for altitude).
Reads one 12-field line into a MissionItem; a line with another number of fields raises ValueError quoting it.
Writes the items to a file: the header 'QGC WPL 110' and one line per item, with Linux line endings and no comments (Mission Planner refuses comments).
Reads a QGC WPL 110 file into MissionItems, skipping blank and '#' lines; a wrong header or bad line raises ValueError.

Builds the team-shaped search mission: item 0 home (frame 0), 1 NAV_TAKEOFF to the survey height, 2 the first lane point, 3 DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL with all-zero values (MAVProxy multiplies x/y by 1e7 on upload), optionally DO_CHANGE_SPEED (ground speed, m/s), the other lane ends, the hold point, and NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH. NAV items use frame 3 (metres above home).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: Home, lane points (lat, lon), altitude, hold point, optional speed

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Works out the indices last year's nodes would derive from this mission, copying their logic: waypoint_manager's takeoff_index, next_after_takeoff, rtl_index, last_before_rtl (rtl - 1) and buffer_wp (rtl - 2, where photos stop); main_controller's last NAV item before RTL (the hold trigger) and its own buffer; every DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL index and the insert index for target waypoints. -1 means not found.

Lists every way a mission breaks the team shape: seq numbers not counting up, item 0 not home, not exactly one TAKEOFF at index 1, RTL not last, a LAND item, R-1 or R-2 not NAV_WAYPOINTs, hold and insert points disagreeing, a missing or misplaced DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL (it must follow TAKEOFF and the first lane point and come before buffer_wp), NAV items not in frame 3, altitudes outside an optional band, or waypoints at latitude/longitude 0. Empty list = all good.

Makes a readable table of the mission, one line per item with command, frame, lat/lon/alt, local x/y (when home is given) and the item's role (takeoff, 'photos START', 'buffer_wp: photos STOP here', 'hold', RTL), plus the speed of DO_CHANGE_SPEED.
Horizontal flight length in metres from home through every NAV_WAYPOINT and back home (the RTL leg).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Turns 'survey this rectangle from this height' into a complete team-shaped mission and reads the survey settings from a world's config file, so a mission can always be re-made from config/<world>.yaml alone (for example at another altitude). It also adds the lead-in: lane 1 starts lead_in_s seconds of flight early because the team's video_cam spends about 15 s on zoom and focus after DigiCamCtrl.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by build_runway.py, build_suas_field.py and make_mission.py.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: How to fly the survey: altitude, sidelap 0.3, frontlap 0.6, photo interval 2 s, speed (None = automatic, 0 = no DO_CHANGE_SPEED item), max speed 10 m/s, camera fov and photo size, overshoot past lane ends and lead_in_s.

Returns the point 'distance_m' metres BEFORE the lane start on the line from the next point through the start (lane 1 made longer at its beginning); the start itself when the distance is 0 or the points coincide.

Plans the lanes over the rectangle (survey.plan_lanes from home), picks the lane speed (automatic from the frontlap, none, or the given one), moves the first lane point back for the lead-in, converts all points to latitude/longitude in ArduPilot's convention and builds the mission with the hold point at the rectangle centre (or hold_xy).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: Home, Rect, SurveySettings, optional hold point

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Makes a survey.Rect from a config 'search_areas' entry {center: [x, y], size: [along lanes, across], yaw}.
Makes SurveySettings from a config 'survey' section (with defaults for missing keys), then applies keyword overrides that are not None (for example altitude from the command line).

Describes a planned mission as a dict: altitude, lanes, spacing, footprint, cm per pixel, speed, survey and total path length, item count, DigiCamCtrl index, buffer_wp, hold and RTL index and lane direction; written into the config's 'planned' block and printed by make_mission.py.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: The camera footprint maths and the lawn-mower survey planner. A straight-down camera at height h with an 81 deg lens sees a ground rectangle 2 x h x tan(40.5 deg) = 1.708 h wide (across the lane) and 1440/2560 of that long; lanes are spaced so neighbours overlap by the sidelap (30 %) and the outer strips end exactly at the area edges; the speed keeps the frontlap (60 %) with one photo every 2 s.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by planner.py to make the search missions; defaults are the team camera (A8 mini lens, 2560x1440 ZR10-profile stills).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The ground rectangle a straight-down camera sees: width_m (across the lane), height_m (along the lane) and gsd_m (metres of ground per pixel at the image centre).

Computes the Footprint at a given height above flat ground: width = 2 x height x tan(hfov / 2), length = width x 1440 / 2560, ground per pixel = width / 2560. Height 0 or less raises ValueError. At 30 m that is 51.2 x 28.8 m and 2.0 cm per pixel.
A rectangle on the ground in local metres: centre (cx, cy), length along the lane direction 'yaw', width across it.
Turns rectangle coordinates (u along the length, v across, measured from the centre) into world x, y by rotating with the yaw.
Turns world x, y into rectangle coordinates (u along the length, v across, from the centre).
The four corners of the rectangle in world coordinates, counter-clockwise.
True when a world point is inside the rectangle shrunk by 'margin' metres on every side.
The result of plan_lanes: waypoints in flight order, the same points grouped per lane, actual and maximum lane spacing, footprint, altitude, sidelap, lane direction, path length and notes.
The number of lanes in the plan.

Plans a lawn-mower survey of a rectangle: lanes along its length, as few as needed so neighbours overlap by at least the sidelap, spread evenly so the outer photo strips end at the edges (one lane if a photo is wider than the area). It tries the four possible starting corners and keeps the one nearest to where the drone comes from (home), then zig-zags. Impossible inputs raise ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: Rect, altitude, sidelap, camera, start point, overshoot

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The fastest lane speed that still gives the wanted frontlap: footprint length x (1 - frontlap) / photo interval, rounded DOWN to 0.5 m/s and kept between 2 and 10 m/s. At 30 m with 60 % frontlap and a photo every 2 s that is 5.5 m/s.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: altitude, frontlap, photo interval, limits, camera

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Reads and checks the answer-key files truth/<world>.yaml and answers 'which target is nearest to this GPS point?'. Class ids match the team detector: person '0', tent '1', object '2'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by check_world.py, worldgen/builder.py (CLASS_IDS) and the tests; sim_demo reads the truth YAML files with its own loader. Never given to the real detector.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Reads a truth YAML file into a dict (empty dict for an empty file).
Returns the target entries, optionally only those of one class ('person' or 'tent').
Returns the truth file's world origin as a geo.Home.

Checks a truth dict: required top-level keys, at least one person and one tent target, every entry has id, class, x/y/z/yaw, lat/lon, size and center_z, no duplicate ids, target classes and class ids match, and each entry's lat/lon agrees with its x/y within 5 cm. Returns the problems (empty = good).
Finds the target (optionally of one class) nearest to a latitude/longitude given in ArduPilot's convention and returns it with the distance in metres, or (None, infinity) when there is none.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: truth dict, lat, lon, optional class

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Finds and reads config/<world>.yaml and turns its relative paths into absolute ones. Required fields: world_file, home, spawn {x, y, z, yaw}, mission, truth; extra ones (world_name, search_areas, survey, gui) are kept.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by world_info.py, make_mission.py and check_world.py. sim_bringup (sim_paths.load_world_config) and sim_demo (its own world_info.py) read the same YAML files with their own code.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns the sim_worlds share folder: the installed package when ROS can find it, else this source tree (when it has a config/ folder); otherwise raises FileNotFoundError telling you to source the workspace.
Names of every world that has a config file, e.g. ['runway', 'suas_field'].

A loaded world config with absolute paths: name, world_name (the SDF's world name used by gz services), world_file, home (geo.Home), spawn, mission, truth, share folder, search_areas, survey and the raw YAML.
A plain dict for printing: name, world name, absolute paths, home as the SITL text and spawn.

Loads a world by name ('runway') or YAML path: checks the required fields and the four spawn values, makes paths absolute (relative to the share folder, or to the YAML's parent folder for a path) and parses home. A missing world or field raises FileNotFoundError / ValueError with the known worlds listed.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: world name or path, optional share

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Keeps an absolute path as is and joins a relative one onto the base folder.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Marks realfield as a Python sub-package and explains the WORK-IN-PROGRESS real-terrain generator 'suas_field_real': stage 1 'prepare' (GIS Python: raw USGS lidar, NAIP photo, OpenStreetMap, building footprints -> prepared grids; prepare.py, trees_detect.py), stage 2 'build' (numpy + Pillow: terrain tiles, ground pictures, trees, buildings; rtin, glb, terrain, texture, trees, structures) and a 'targets' step. It also names a sampler.py that is not in the folder on disk.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Front end is scripts/build_real_field.py; site.py holds every real-world number. Nothing here is used by the runway / suas_field worlds or by a normal simulator run.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Saves a ground picture as a compressed DDS texture (BC1 / DXT1 with a full mipmap chain) using only numpy and Pillow, and can decode it back. A 2048 x 2048 JPG takes about 22 MB of graphics memory in Gazebo, the same picture as BC1 about 2.8 MB, which matters on the laptop's shared 8 GB GPU that the YOLO detector also needs.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Meant for the sharp search-area terrain pictures of the WIP real-terrain world (stage 3).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Packs RGB colours (0-255) into 16-bit RGB565 numbers (5 bits red, 6 green, 5 blue).
Unpacks RGB565 numbers back into RGB colours scaled to 0-255.

Encodes an RGB picture (sides multiples of 4) as BC1 blocks: for every 4 x 4 block it finds the main colour direction, picks two end colours a little inside the extremes, and stores for each pixel which of the 4 palette colours is nearest (2 bits each).
Builds the 128-byte DDS file header for a DXT1 texture of the given size and number of mipmap levels.

Saves an RGB picture (power-of-two sides) as a BC1 DDS file with every mipmap level down to 1 x 1 (each half size, box-filtered), encoding in strips of 256 rows, written to a .part file and renamed. Returns the file size.
Decodes the top (full-size) mipmap level of a BC1 DDS written by write_dds_bc1 back into an RGB picture, for checks and previews.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Writes and inspects binary glTF 2.0 mesh files (.glb) with numpy only. Vertices are written directly in Gazebo's frame (x east, y north, z UP), texture v points down (glTF rule), triangles counter-clockwise from outside; GLB loads much faster in Gazebo than OBJ or COLLADA.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Output format of the real-terrain terrain tiles, trees and buildings (WIP stage 3).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes a .glb file from mesh primitives (positions, optional normals and texture coordinates, triangle indices, optional material index) and optional simple PBR materials, using 16-bit indices when a primitive has fewer than 65,536 vertices. Returns the file size.
Appends one array's bytes (padded to 4 bytes) to the binary chunk and records a buffer view for it; returns the view's index.
Reads only the JSON part of a .glb (to count vertices and triangles without loading geometry); raises ValueError if it is not a glTF 2.0 binary file.
Summarises a .glb: total vertices and triangles, bounding box, number of primitives and file size.
Reads all vertex positions and triangles of a .glb written by write_glb into two numpy arrays (used by the checks).
Reads one accessor's numbers out of the binary blob with the right type (float, uint32 or uint16) and shape.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: The simple file format between the two generator stages: stage 1 saves every north-up raster on the WORLD grid as a NumPy .npy file and lists it in prepared/grid.json (x0 = left edge, y1 = top edge, res = metres per pixel); stage 2 reads them back (memory-mapped) with no GDAL needed.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by prepare.py, pack.py, trees_detect.py and sitepack.py (WIP real-terrain world).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: One raster: its data array (possibly memory-mapped) and its placement in the world (x0, y1, res, description, no-data value).
Stores the data and the placement numbers.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: data, x0, y1, res, what, nodata

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Number of rows (north to south).
Number of columns (west to east).
The raster's world box (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max) in metres.
Fractional (column, row) of world points, measured from pixel centres (a whole number = a pixel centre).
Bilinear value at world points (blending the 4 nearest pixels); points outside are clamped to the edge; works for one band or all bands.
The integer pixel window (r0, r1, c0, c1) covering a world box plus some padding, clipped to the raster.
Bilinear samples on a grid of x values (west to east) and y values (north to south).
All prepared rasters and metadata of one data folder (prepared/grid.json), with a cache of loaded rasters.
Reads prepared/grid.json; raises FileNotFoundError telling you to run 'build_real_field.py prepare' first when it is missing.
True when a raster was prepared and its file exists (optional layers may be missing).
Loads a prepared raster ('dtm', 'naip', 'chm', ...) as a Raster, memory-mapped by default, and caches it.
Absolute path of a non-raster prepared file listed in the metadata (trees.csv, features.json).
Saves one raster as <name>_<res>m.npy (e.g. dtm_0p5m.npy) and registers its placement, shape, type and description in the grid.json dict.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: folder, meta dict, name, array, x0, y1, res, what, nodata

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes prepared/grid.json pretty-printed with sorted keys so changes stay readable.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Generator stage 2 ('pack'): turns the big prepared grids of stage 1 (not in git) into the compact committed SITE PACK data/suas_field_real/ (about 12 MB): 1 m heights with the pad square levelled, ground colour at 0.25 m near the search areas and 1 m elsewhere (grass graded to competition-week colour, the new wetland and pipeline lane repainted, crowns of 3D trees painted out), ground classes for the search areas, closed-forest canopy heights, trees.csv with crown colours, features.json, CC0 detail pictures, pack.json and LICENSES.md. Needs numpy, scipy and Pillow.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Run by 'build_real_field.py pack'; its output is what sitepack.SitePack reads (WIP real-terrain world).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns <package>/data/suas_field_real, where the site pack goes.
Returns the world boxes around all non-far terrain tiles (the 'near' zone) and around all detail tiles.
Bounding box (x0, y0, x1, y1) of a list of tiles.
Top-left corner and pixel counts (x0, y1, cols, rows) of a north-up grid covering a box plus a margin at a resolution.
Cuts the block of a prepared raster whose top-left pixel corner is exactly (x0, y1); raises ValueError if it reaches outside the raster.
Averages f x f pixel blocks (shrinks a raster by a whole factor).
World x, y of every pixel centre of a grid, as two 2-D arrays.
Distance in metres from every grid point to a polyline (road, runway, pipeline), skipping segments more than 50 m from the whole window so 100+ roads stay fast.
Even-odd inside test of a polygon for whole arrays of points (used for water areas).

Picks the grass colour multipliers (R, G, B): the grade stage 1 measured from Sentinel-2 if it is sensible (each factor 0.6-1.3), otherwise the fallback site.GRASS_GRADE_RGB (0.77, 0.88, 0.79); returns where it came from too.

Steps 1-3 on one picture window: multiplies grass pixels (weighted by NDVI, never crowns) by the season grade, repaints the new wetland west of Search Boundary 1 wet and green, lightens the buried-pipeline lane, and paints out the crowns of trees that become 3D models with the colour of the nearest open sunlit ground (only where the area is mostly open), then smooths.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: RGB+NIR window, coordinates, crown mask, paint-out mask, features, log, tag, resolution, grade

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Gives every pixel of a window a ground class: grass by default, dry grass (low NDVI, bright), bare soil (very low NDVI, bright, reddish), gravel along roads and taxiways, asphalt along the runway, water inside water polygons, canopy for crowns, under_tree for painted-out crowns, wetland inside the new wetland.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: RGB, NDVI, crown, painted, X, Y, features

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Saves a 16-bit greyscale PNG (the height picture).
Saves an 8-bit PNG (classes, canopy, detail maps).
Saves a JPEG with normal 4:2:0 colour subsampling (colour finer than 0.5 m is not in the NAIP photo anyway).
Turns a CC0 colour texture into a seamless 'brightness detail' map: grey value divided by its own wrap-around blur, scaled so 99 % of pixels fall within the amplitude, stored with 128 = unchanged.

Runs stage 2: reads prepared/grid.json, sets home at the pad with the DTM median height rounded to 0.1 m, then writes height_1m.png (pad levelled), colour_near_0p25m.jpg and class_detail_0p25m.png, colour_far_1m.jpg (processed in strips), canopy_1m.png (closed forest + growth), trees.csv with each crown's photo colour, features.json, the detail pictures, pack.json and LICENSES.md, and logs sizes and statistics.
Marks on a grid every pixel inside the crown disk (+0.75 m) of a tree that will be a 3D model, so its paint can be removed from the ground picture.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: grid x0, y1, cols, rows, res

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes the pack's LICENSES.md table: what each file is derived from (USGS lidar, NAIP, Meta/WRI canopy, OKMaps mask, Sentinel-2, OpenStreetMap ODbL, Microsoft CDLA, Poly Haven CC0), its licence and the credit to give; notes that Google imagery is not used.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Generator stage 1 ('prepare', needs a GIS Python: rasterio, pyproj, laspy, scipy): reprojects the raw downloads from three map projections onto ONE world grid (origin = the Runway 2 pad) and saves them for stage 2: dtm (0.5 m bare earth, with the vanished soil piles levelled and the new wetland dug), chm (0.5 m canopy height from the lidar point cloud with floating 'haze' dropped and spikes removed), naip (0.25 m R, G, B, NIR photo), optional leafoff evergreen mask and Meta canopy heights, the Sentinel-2 season grade, features.json (OSM + Microsoft buildings with lidar heights) and trees.csv (via trees_detect).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Run by 'build_real_field.py prepare' into ~/.astra_sim/world_data/suas_field_real/prepared (never committed).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns the root, raw and prepared folders of the real field's data: $ASTRA_WORLD_DATA or ~/.astra_sim/world_data, then suas_field_real/raw and /prepared.
Finds data/real_field_manifest.json in the source tree or the installed share folder (FileNotFoundError otherwise).
Reads the data manifest (sources with URLs, checksums and licences) into a dict.
Lists the raw files of one manifest layer ('dtm', 'lidar', 'naip', ...) that exist, in manifest order.
Top-left corner and size (x0, y1, cols, rows) of a north-up world raster at a resolution covering the terrain EXTENT plus an 8 m margin.

Reprojects one or more GeoTIFFs onto the world grid (Transverse Mercator centred on the pad) band by band with rasterio; later files only fill cells the earlier ones left empty, and each band goes straight into the output type to save memory.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: files, bands, res, resampling, dtype, source no-data, fill, margin

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Fills empty (NaN) cells with the value of the nearest valid cell and reports what share was filled.
Weight 1 inside a box falling smoothly (cosine) to 0 at 'feather' metres outside it; used to blend edits and the levelled pad into the ground.

Patches the 2017 ground where it is out of date (site.DTM_EDITS): levels the three vanished soil piles south-east of Search Boundary 1 with a 41 m grey opening inside a feathered box, and digs the new wetland west of SB1 as a smooth 0.8 m bowl (an estimate). Records how much was lowered and removed.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: DTM array, x0, y1, res, meta, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Reprojects the USGS 3DEP DTM tiles (0.5 m, NAD83 UTM 15N, NAVD88) onto the world grid, fills gaps, applies the edits, sets the home height = median DTM height over the 12.2 m pad square, and saves the raster.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: raw folder, manifest, output folder, meta, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Reads the lidar point clouds (LAZ) in chunks, drops noise classes, withheld points and 'haze' more than 35 m above the bare earth, keeps the highest return per 0.5 m cell, subtracts the ground, clips at 40 m and flattens single-cell spikes, then saves the canopy height model and the cleaning statistics.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: raw folder, manifest, output folder, meta, DTM Raster, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: World x, y of every pixel centre of a grid, as two 2-D arrays.
Reprojects the NAIP 2023 photo (0.3 m, R, G, B, NIR, UTM 14N) onto the 0.25 m world grid with cubic resampling and saves it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: raw folder, manifest, output folder, meta, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Optional: turns the OKMaps 2025 leaf-off photo into a 0.5 m yes/no 'evergreen-looking in March' mask (dark and not reddish = eastern red-cedar). Only the mask is kept, because the photo's licence does not allow redistribution; returns None if not downloaded.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: raw folder, manifest, output folder, meta, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Optional fallback: reprojects the Meta/WRI 2019 canopy height map onto a 1 m world grid (CC-BY 4.0); returns None if not downloaded.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: raw folder, manifest, output folder, meta, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns the BOA_ADD_OFFSET of a Sentinel-2 L2A scene: the manifest's value if given, else -1000 for processing baseline N0400 or later found in the product name, else -1000.
Vegetation index NDVI = (NIR - red) / (NIR + red) of an R, G, B, NIR array.
Median ratio new / old per colour band over a mask, returned clipped to 0.6-1.3 and unclipped; (None, None) when the mask is empty.
For every 10 m Sentinel-2 cell, the share of NAIP pixels that look like sunlit grass (NDVI 0.08-0.36 and brightness 70-150), computed in blocks of rows.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: NAIP Raster, rows, cols, factor, block

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Optional: measures how much greener/darker the grass was on competition day (Sentinel-2 2026) than in the NAIP week (2023), after removing the +1000 storage offset, as per-band median ratios over pure-grass cells (at least 50 cells, else a looser mask, else none). Records the result and two comparison numbers in meta['season_grade'].
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: raw folder, manifest, meta, NAIP Raster, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The first version's 'grass-like' NDVI band rule for both years (kept to compare results).
Signed area of a polygon ring (positive = counter-clockwise).
Gives every building footprint the median lidar canopy height inside it ('height_lidar') and its 90th percentile; footprints with a median below 2 m (probably built after 2017) get no lidar height.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.effects: adds keys to the building dicts

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Turns the OpenStreetMap Overpass JSON into world-metre buildings, water areas, streams, runway, taxiways, pipelines and roads, adds Microsoft building footprints that OSM does not already have, adds lidar building heights, and writes features.json with the licence notes.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: raw folder, manifest, output folder, meta, Home, log, CHM

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Even-odd point-in-polygon test for one point.

Runs the whole prepare stage in order: DTM (and home height), canopy model (or reuse it with --skip-lidar), NAIP, leaf-off mask, Meta canopy, season grade, features, tree detection; then records the sources and time and writes grid.json.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.effects: writes the prepared rasters, trees.csv, features.json and grid.json

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Simplifies a square height grid (2^k + 1 points per side) into a triangle mesh that never differs from the grid by more than a chosen height error (RTIN, the 'Martini' method by Vladimir Agafonkin, re-written with numpy): flat grass gets few triangles, ditches and banks many. Forced points (tile borders) are always kept, so neighbouring tiles join without gaps.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by terrain.py to make the real-terrain tiles and collision mesh.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The precomputed hierarchy of right triangles for an n x n grid (n = 2^k + 1), grouped by level from the smallest triangles up.
Checks the grid size is 2^k + 1 (else ValueError) and computes, for every triangle id, the corner points of its long side, sorted by level (vectorised).
Returns a cached hierarchy for a grid size (building it once).

Computes the error of every grid point: how far the height at the middle of each triangle's long side is from the straight line between its corners, inheriting the largest error of the smaller triangles inside; forced points get infinite error.
Walks down the triangle tree and splits a triangle only while its error is above max_error, giving the used grid points and the triangles.
A boolean n x n grid that is True on the outer ring (to force tile borders).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Every number that describes the REAL SUAS 2026 field (Skyway36, north Tulsa) and the world frame of 'suas_field_real', with sources: origin = the Runway 2 VTOL pad at 36.2147411, -96.0067230 (about 50 m from the procedural world's origin), the paved strip 02/20, Runway 1, the flight boundary and search boundaries from the Team Handbook, altitude rules (150-400 ft), the grass colour fallback, the sun direction, three hand-added wooden poles in Search Boundary 1 and an unconfirmed wire, the ground edits, and the terrain tile layout (264 m blocks split into 132 m and 66 m tiles near the action).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by every realfield module; needs only sim_worlds.geo.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns the world origin (the pad) as a geo.Home at a given ground height (NAVD88 metres from the DTM).
WGS84 latitude/longitude -> world x east, y north on the exact local tangent plane (what Gazebo uses).
World x, y -> exact WGS84 latitude/longitude (inverse of world_xy).
Returns the PROJ text of the world frame for GIS tools: Transverse Mercator on WGS84 centred on the pad with scale 1 (matches the tangent plane to under 1 cm over this field).
The 11 flight-boundary corners in world metres.
A search boundary as a world box (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max).
The hand-added structures (the three poles) with their world x, y added.
The paved strip's south end, north end and unit direction (south to north) in world metres.
Shortest distance between two axis-aligned rectangles (0 when they touch or overlap).
True when a rectangle overlaps a box grown by a margin with a real area (only sharing an edge does not count).

Lays out the terrain tiles over the 1848 m square: a 264 m block more than 100 m from both search boundaries and the pad stays one 'far' tile; otherwise it becomes four 132 m 'near' quads; a quad touching a search boundary (or within 30 m of the pad) becomes four 66 m tiles, 'detail' where they overlap that zone, else 'near66'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.outputs: list of tile dicts sorted by name

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: True when a block is within 100 m of a search boundary or of the pad.
True when a box overlaps a search boundary or the pad's 30 m square.
True when a point is within a margin (default 100 m) of a search boundary or of the pad (used for tree and building detail levels).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Reads the committed SITE PACK data/suas_field_real/ with numpy and Pillow only: pack.json, the 16-bit height picture, the far and near colour pictures, the ground-class picture, the forest canopy picture, trees.csv, features.json and the CC0 detail pictures, all in world metres around the Runway 2 pad. Typical use: SitePack().ground_z(x, y).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: The input of the WIP stages 3 and 4; terrain, texture, trees and structures read the pack through it.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns <package>/data/suas_field_real in the source tree when it has pack.json, else the installed share folder's copy, else the source path.
Loads a PNG or JPG as a numpy array (16-bit for 16-bit PNGs), with Pillow's size limit switched off for these big own files.
The site pack in a folder: its metadata, home (geo.Home) and a cache of decoded rasters and files.
Reads pack.json from the folder (default the package's) and builds the home; raises FileNotFoundError when the pack is missing.
Absolute path of a file inside the pack.

Loads one pack raster as a grids.Raster with decoded values: 'height' (metres NAVD88 = 150 + value x 0.01), 'colour_far' / 'colour_near' (RGB), 'class' (codes), 'canopy' (metres = value x 0.125); cached.
Ground height (metres NAVD88) at world points, bilinear in the 1 m height raster (the same surface the terrain meshes follow).
Ground height at world points as world z (metres above the pad = home altitude).
Reads trees.csv into a list of dicts with numbers converted (x, y, ground height, height, crown diameter, forest flag); cached.
Reads features.json (buildings, water, streams, runways, taxiways, roads, pipelines); cached.
The list of CC0 detail pictures from pack.json (name, file, real size in metres, use, amplitude).
Loads one detail picture as a brightness multiplier array (1.0 = unchanged, from 128 = neutral and the picture's amplitude); cached.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: The man-made things of the real field from the site pack: about 400 BUILDINGS (OpenStreetMap + Microsoft footprints raised to their lidar roof height, else OSM height/levels, else Microsoft height, else 4 m) merged into one mesh per shadow group with a tiny colour-palette picture and real roof colours, plus the hand-added wooden poles in Search Boundary 1 and the optional wire as simple SDF shapes.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Part of the WIP real-terrain world's stage 3/4.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Picks a building's height and says where it came from: lidar 2017 median, else a height tag (Microsoft or OSM), else OSM levels x 3 m + 1 m, else the default 4 m.
Twice the signed area of a polygon (positive = counter-clockwise).
Cuts a simple polygon (a roof outline) into triangles by repeatedly clipping 'ears', returning counter-clockwise triangles; falls back to a fan for broken rings.
True when the corner i1 is convex and no other remaining point lies inside the triangle (i0, i1, i2), so it can be cut off.
The mean photo colour inside a building footprint (from the near or far colour picture).
Texture coordinate of the centre of a palette cell (cell 0 = walls, 1-15 = roof colour groups).
Makes the 64 x 64 palette picture: 4 x 4 cells of 16 pixels, cell 0 the wall colour, then the roof group colours.
True when a point is within 150 m of a search boundary or the pad (those buildings cast shadows).

Builds the merged building meshes: keeps footprints inside the terrain, gives each a height and roof colour, groups roof colours into 15 brightness groups, makes walls (one quad per edge from below ground to the roof) and a triangulated flat roof, and splits them into a 'near' (shadow-casting) and 'far' mesh. Returns the meshes, the palette picture and one info dict per building.
SDF parts of one wooden pole standing on the ground and sunk 0.5 m into it, with cylinder collision.
A sagging cable between two points as a chain of thin cylinders following a parabola.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: p0, p1, sag, diameter, segments, name

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: The ground of the real-terrain world as Gazebo meshes from the site pack heights: one mesh per terrain tile (65 x 65 grid simplified by RTIN to 5 cm error in the search areas, 10 cm near them, 25 cm far away), every border point kept, short vertical 'skirts' hiding cracks, normals from the 1 m height raster and texture coordinates matching each tile's picture; plus one coarser merged collision mesh for the flight boundary + 150 m (a Gazebo heightmap misbehaved on this laptop).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Part of the WIP real-terrain world's stage 3.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Makes a function mapping world points to texture coordinates for a tile picture whose first and last pixel centres sit exactly on the tile edges, so neighbouring tiles show the same colour on their shared edge.
Computes (u, v) for world points inside the tile.
The full 65 x 65 grid of a tile: x values west to east, y values north to south and the ground z at each point.
Ground normals (unit vectors) at points from central differences of the height raster.
Flips triangles that are clockwise seen from above so every face points up.
Makes the RTIN mesh of one tile at a tolerance with every border point kept.
The edges used by only one triangle (the mesh outline), in each triangle's own direction.

Builds the visual mesh of one tile: simplified surface, normals, texture coordinates, and a skirt (0.6-1.5 m deep depending on tile kind) hanging below every border edge; returns the mesh primitive and triangle counts.
Selects the tiles within 150 m of the flight boundary's bounding box (those get physics).
Builds one merged collision mesh over those tiles at the per-kind collision tolerance, merging duplicated border vertices and dropping degenerate triangles.
Ground slope in degrees at points, from the height raster.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Paints each terrain tile's picture (and the forest canopy sheets) from the site pack: the real NAIP colour (season graded, tree crowns painted out) and, in the search areas, centimetre ground detail from CC0 pictures laid at their real size and blended by ground class, so the ground still looks like ground in a 3-4 cm per pixel drone photo. An optional colour_override hook can swap in another licence-compatible picture.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Part of the WIP real-terrain world's stage 3; trees.py also uses sample_colour.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: A cached Pillow image of a pack colour raster ('colour_near' or 'colour_far').
Computes the Pillow resize box (in source pixels) that puts the output pixel centres exactly from one tile edge to the other, and the scale factor.
True when one box lies inside another (with a tiny tolerance).
The RGB picture of a world box at a pixel size, from the 0.25 m near picture when the box is inside it, else from the 1 m picture.
For a box, a weight map per ground class present (smooth 25 cm transitions); only grass when the box is outside the class picture.
Samples a detail picture laid over the world at its real size, rotated, pre-shrunk so one texel is about one output pixel, with wrap-around bilinear lookup (1.0 = no change).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: SitePack, detail name, X, Y, rotation, output resolution

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The brightness multiplier (about 1.0 on average) for a box: for each class present, the product of its RECIPE detail layers, blended by the class weights.
The picture of one terrain tile: the override colour if given, else the sampled photo colour, multiplied by the micro detail when the tile kind wants it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: SitePack, tile, pixels, micro flag, optional override

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: The REAL trees of the field as Gazebo meshes from trees.csv: each tree is a copy of a small low-poly shape (deciduous lumpy ellipsoid or red-cedar lumpy cone) stretched to its real height and crown, turned randomly, set on the real ground; all trees of a 264 m block are merged into one crown mesh (+ trunks near the action) with one shared leaf 'atlas' picture of 8 tones taken from real crown colours; no collision. Closed forest becomes one canopy sheet per block at the lidar canopy height with walls to the ground.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Part of the WIP real-terrain world's stage 3 (merging made 2,000 trees load in 3.5 s instead of 30 s).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Builds a closed surface of revolution from rings at given heights and radii with lumpy radius noise: positions, outward normals, texture coordinates (u around, v down from the top) and outward-facing triangles.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: ring heights, radii, segments, generator, lumpiness

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: A unit crown (diameter 1, height 1): a narrow lumpy cone for cedars or a lumpy ellipsoid from 0.24 to 1.0 of the height for deciduous trees, with more rings near the action than far away.
A unit trunk: a thin 6-sided prism from the ground into the crown (0.30 of the height for deciduous, 0.12 for cedars).
Turns a hex colour like '3e573f' into an RGB array.
For deciduous trees and cedars, 4 tone colours each (medians of the brightness quartiles of the real crown colours) and a function telling which atlas cell a tree uses.
Returns the atlas (row, column) of a tree: row 0 deciduous / 1 cedar, column = its crown colour's brightness quartile.
Paints the 4 x 2 cell crown picture (256 px cells) of procedural leaf-clump texture in the tone colours, with dark gaps between clumps (made here, so no licence issue).
Stretches a unit shape to a crown diameter and height, turns it by yaw and moves it to a position (normals adjusted too).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: shape positions, normals, diameter, height, yaw, xyz

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The ground height under a trunk: the lowest of the centre and four points around it, sunk 0.25 m so trees never float on slopes.
The (i, j) index of the 264 m terrain block containing a world point.

Merges all non-forest trees per block: picks one of 3 shape variants per tree, stretches and places it on the ground, gives it its atlas cell, adds trunks in near blocks, and returns one crown mesh (and trunk mesh) per block with counts, plus the tones and atlas picture.

Builds the closed-forest canopy sheet of one block: a 3 m grid at ground + canopy height where the canopy is above 0.5 m, with normals, texture coordinates and walls down to the ground along its edges, plus its 512 px photo texture; (None, None) without forest.
The texture-coordinate function of a block picture (first and last pixel centres on the block edges), using terrain.texel_uv.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Finds the REAL trees of the field (part of stage 1, numpy + scipy) and writes prepared/trees.csv plus the 2023 crown mask and the closed-forest mask: tree tops from the 2017 lidar canopy envelope (3-31 m, not on roofs), crown size by 8 rays, crowns in the September 2023 photo by a calibrated colour rule, lidar trees kept only if still visible in 2023, new trees from photo blobs confirmed by Meta 2019 or a young lidar tree, cedar vs deciduous from the March 2025 leaf-off mask, and growth estimated to September 2026.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Called by prepare.run; pack.py reads its outputs (WIP real-terrain world).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The local-maximum window for a tree of height h: 2 m + 0.35 x h, kept between 3 and 12 m.
Estimated height growth over some years: 0.30 m/year under 10 m, 0.22 under 16 m, else 0.12, capped at 3 m (works on arrays).

Marks the 2023 tree-crown pixels of the NAIP photo with the calibrated rule (NDVI >= 0.32, brightness <= 95 and NIR >= 100, or NDVI >= 0.38 and brightness <= 110) on a lightly smoothed photo, in row blocks, then removes specks.
Cuts the raster window around a world point and marks which of its pixels lie inside a circle of the given radius.
Share of True pixels of a mask raster inside a disk (0 outside the raster).
Sets to True the pixels of a mask whose centres are within a radius of a point.
Marks the grid pixels inside building footprints, grown by a margin.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: buildings, grid x0, y1, cols, rows, res, grow

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Finds tree tops in the 0.5 m canopy model: builds a 1 m crown envelope (highest point per cell, grey closing, 1 m blur), keeps points at least 3 m high that are the highest inside a height-dependent window, and measures each crown radius as the median length of 8 rays that stop where the canopy drops below 45 % of the top or rises into a neighbour.

Finds NEW trees seen only in the 2023 photo: crown blobs not explained by kept lidar trees or roofs, one tree at the fattest point of a blob within 10 m windows and at least 6 m apart, crown = the patch of blob pixels nearest to it; a tree is kept only if large enough and confirmed by the Meta 2019 canopy (>= 2 m) or a young 2017 lidar tree (>= 1 m).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: crown mask, its Raster, kept trees, Meta CHM, envelope, roof mask, log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Counts trees from the lidar and from the photo in the flight boundary and in each search boundary.

Runs the tree detection: lidar tops minus noise and roofs, the 2023 crown mask, which lidar trees are still there, new photo trees, then each tree's 2026 height, crown and kind (cedar or deciduous), the closed-forest mask (never within 30 m of a search area), and writes trees.csv, the 'forest' and 'crown2023' rasters and statistics in meta['trees'].
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: output folder, meta, DTM, CHM, NAIP, leaf-off mask, Meta CHM, Home, log, buildings
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.effects: writes trees.csv, forest and crown2023 rasters

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: World x, y of the pixel centres of a Raster, as two 2-D arrays.
The fraction of True pixels of a fine mask inside each pixel of a coarser grid that shares the same corner (whole-number resolution ratio).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Marks worldgen as a Python sub-package and lists its building blocks: sdf (parts to SDF text), assets (pinned Fuel models), primitives (simple-shape objects), meshes (OBJ writers), textures (painted pictures), layout (no-overlap placement) and world (header, GUI). Needs numpy and Pillow, only to re-generate worlds.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by scripts/build_runway.py and build_suas_field.py; not needed to run the simulator.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: The catalogue of realistic Gazebo Fuel models the worlds use, at PINNED versions, with measured placement and bounding boxes: the hiker (Rescue Randy mannequin) standing, lying face up, lying face down and sitting; four standing people; hatchback, SUV and pickup; oak and pine trees (bushes are small oaks); cone, construction barrel, 55-gallon drum, folding chair and table, and a pop-up canopy. The worlds reference the Fuel MESH files inside our own static models, because the Fuel models themselves are not usable as they are (not static, floating links, extra plugins, none lie down).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by builder.py (add_asset, trees) and the generators; scripts/fetch_models.sh must list the same 17 models (a unit test checks). CC-BY models are credited in the README.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: One Fuel model at a pinned version: owner, name, version and licence (CC0 or CC-BY 4.0).
The model's download URL https://fuel.gazebosim.org/1.0/<owner>/models/<name>/<version>, what 'gz fuel download -u' takes.
The URL of one file inside the model (lower-case owner and name, as Fuel's own SDF files write it), e.g. .../rescue randy/3/files/meshes/rescue_randy.dae.
One mesh visual of an asset: mesh file inside the Fuel model, position and rotation in the asset frame, scale, optional sub-mesh name and optional material maps (None keeps the mesh's own colours).

A placeable object made of Fuel meshes: our key, the Fuel model, its visuals, the bounding box in its own frame (ground at z = 0, measured and checked in side-view renders), its kind (mannequin, person, vehicle, tree, prop, canopy), the class the team detector would give it ('person' or 'object') and a description.
Bounding-box size [sx, sy, sz] in metres at a scale (one number or a 3-number tuple), rounded to millimetres.
Centre of the bounding box (x, y, z) in the asset's own frame at a scale.
Radius of a top-view circle around the asset origin that contains the whole object (used by the Placer to keep objects apart).
Turns a scale given as one number into (s, s, s) and checks a tuple has exactly 3 values (else ValueError).
Returns the four Rescue Randy texture paths (albedo, normal, roughness, metalness pictures) used as its material.
Looks up an Asset by key; an unknown key raises KeyError listing the known keys.

Makes the parts that draw an asset at a scale: one mesh part per Fuel visual (pinned file URL, scale, sub-mesh, material maps, tint, double-sided leaves) and, with collision=True, one invisible collision box around the whole object so physics stays cheap and a payload can land on it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: key, scale, collision flag, name prefix

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: The sorted unique Fuel models behind some asset keys (what fetch_models.sh must download).
The four top-view corners (world x, y) of an asset placed at (x, y) with heading yaw and a scale.
Every Fuel model in the catalogue.
Sanity check for the unit tests: every bounding box is non-empty and starts at the ground (z min = 0).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Collects everything that goes into one world (objects, grass patches, trees, search areas, the hiker and the tent) in a WorldBuilder and writes the four files of a world: worlds/<name>.sdf, config/<name>.yaml, truth/<name>.yaml and missions/<name>_survey.waypoints. It also writes the models shared by all worlds (grass ground, pad, runway, patch pictures, pop-up tent) with a FIXED texture seed 2026.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: The engine of build_runway.py and build_suas_field.py; it uses assets, primitives, sdf, meshes, textures, world, planner and mission.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes a shared model's model.sdf (a static model with one link holding the given body, and a PURPOSE comment saying it is generated) and its model.config (name, version, author, description).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: model folder, name, link body text, purpose, description

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes the models every world uses into models/: sim_worlds_ground (12 km square: a physics plane plus a mesh on which a 4096 px grass picture repeats every 160 m), sim_worlds_pad (12.2 m concrete slab with an H), sim_worlds_runway (152.4 x 12.2 m asphalt), sim_worlds_decals (2 lush, 3 dry and 3 dirt patch pictures and a unit quad) and sim_worlds_tent (dome mesh and 6 fabric colours). Pictures are painted only when missing unless force is set; leftover files of an old tile experiment are removed.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.effects: writes meshes, pictures, model.sdf and model.config files

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Joins path parts under the models folder, creates that folder if needed and returns it.
True when a picture must be painted: force is set or the file does not exist yet.
Parts of the open pop-up tent in one of the six colours, pointing at the shared dome mesh and fabric picture (model:// paths, or paths relative to the tent model folder).
Offline fallback tree: a cylinder trunk and three dark-green ellipsoid crowns, about the given height.

Collects one world and writes its files: name, home, seed, asset mode ('fuel' or 'primitive'), objects, patches, tree groups, includes, search areas, spawn (0, 0, 0.25 m, yaw pi/2 = nose north), GUI camera, follow offset (-12, 0, 6 m), extra truth facts and the set of Fuel assets used.
Stores the world's name, home, seed, asset mode (anything other than fuel/primitive raises ValueError) and description, and sets empty lists plus the default spawn, GUI camera and follow offset.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: name, Home, seed, asset mode, description

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Adds one static object made of parts at (x, y, z, yaw) with its role ('target' must be found, 'distractor' is listed in the truth file, 'scenery' is not), detector class, kind, area, bounding box and extra facts. Duplicate names raise ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: name, parts, pose, role, class, kind, area, size, centre, model, meta, description

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Adds a catalogue asset: in fuel mode (or without a fallback) its Fuel mesh parts and measured box, remembering the asset as used; in primitive mode the fallback's simple-shape parts. The detector class, kind and description come from the catalogue.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: asset key, name, pose, scale, role, area, collision, meta, fallback

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Adds the hiker as a TARGET of class 'person' in one of the poses: the Rescue Randy asset hiker_<pose> in fuel mode, or a simple-shapes mannequin with random clothes colours in primitive mode.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: pose, name, x, y, yaw, area, meta

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Adds the open pop-up tent as a TARGET of class 'tent' (2.4 x 2.2 x 1.35 m, door open on +x) in the given colour.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: name, x, y, yaw, colour, area, meta

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Adds a ground patch picture ('dry', 'lush' or 'dirt') of a given size and rotation; the picture variant wraps around the available ones.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: kind, x, y, size, yaw, variant
