fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Adds an oak or pine tree to a named group (each group becomes one static model); a low wide scale turns an oak into a bush.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: group, asset key, x, y, yaw, scale

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Adds an <include> of a shared model (ground, pad, runway, creek) at a pose.
Declares a search area rectangle; it goes into the config and truth files and a mission is planned over it.
Returns the rectangle of a declared search area (KeyError if unknown).
Makes the one static model 'ground_patches' holding every patch as a textured quad a few centimetres above the grass (lush 4.0, dry 4.8, dirt 5.6 cm, plus tiny steps) so they never flicker.
Makes one static model trees_<group> per tree group, with every tree's parts rotated and moved into place (Fuel meshes without collision, or primitive trees offline).
Builds the complete world file text: header with the GUI, the includes, the patch model, every object (with a TARGET / DISTRACTOR comment) and the tree models, then the closing tags.

Makes one truth-file entry for an object: id, class and class id, kind, description, area, x/y/z/yaw, latitude/longitude in ArduPilot's convention and in WGS84, altitude, bounding box, world position of the box centre, distance from home, model and any extra facts.

Builds the whole truth dictionary: world name, generator facts, frame and lat/lon convention notes, home, class ids, search areas with corners in metres and latitude/longitude, targets, distractors, counts and the extra facts.

Writes worlds/<name>.sdf, plans and writes each mission (the first with no suffix is the contract mission; a mission that breaks the team shape raises RuntimeError), writes truth/<name>.yaml with a header comment and config/<name>.yaml, and returns the written paths and mission summaries.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: package folder, purpose lines, list of (area, suffix, SurveySettings)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.effects: writes the world, missions, truth and config files

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes the config/<name>.yaml text by hand so every field has a comment: world name, description, world file, home, spawn, mission, truth, GUI follow settings, search areas, the survey settings with the planned facts and any extra missions.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Decides WHERE objects go without overlapping, reproducibly: the Placer keeps a list of taken circles and finds free random spots inside a rectangle (optionally rotated, with extra rules such as 'at least 30 m from the tent'), using the numpy random generator you pass so the same seed gives the same layout.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by build_runway.py and build_suas_field.py to place targets and distractors.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Finds free spots in a rectangle: remembers the random generator, the rectangle's bounds (and an inside test for a rotated survey.Rect), the edge inset and the taken circles.
Stores the generator and rectangle; for a rotated survey.Rect it uses the corners' bounding box plus the rectangle's own inside test.
True when a circle of radius r at (x, y) keeps 'gap' metres from every taken circle.
Marks a circle as taken (for objects placed by hand, like the pad area or the bush next to the hiker).

Tries up to 600 random spots inside the rectangle (kept away from the edges by the insets and radius) and returns the first that is free and passes the extra rule, reserving it. Raises RuntimeError when the area is too crowded.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: radius, gap, inset, tries, extra rule

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Writes the few small 3D meshes the worlds need as Wavefront OBJ text files (metres, z up): a flat ground grid whose texture repeats every N metres, a textured quad for patches and pad/runway tops, a ribbon following a line (the creek) and the pop-up dome tent with an open door.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by builder.write_shared_models and build_suas_field.write_creek_model.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes an OBJ file (vertices, texture coordinates, normals, triangles) plus a one-line white .mtl material next to it so Gazebo does not warn 'Missing material' (the SDF material replaces it anyway).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: path, vertices, uvs, normals, faces, comment

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes a flat square grid centred on the origin (e.g. 12 km wide with 1 km cells) whose texture coordinates repeat every repeat_m metres, because an SDF plane cannot repeat a picture.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: path, half size, cell size, repeat distance

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes one textured square facing up at height z, with the picture upright for a north-up camera (a textured SDF box would turn it by 90 degrees).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: path, size x, size y, comment, z

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes a strip of the given width that follows a centre line at height z, with the texture repeating along it every repeat_m metres (the 9 m wide creek).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: path, centre line, width, z, repeat, comment

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes the pop-up dome tent: half an ellipsoid with semi-axes a, b and height c standing on the ground, texture u around the tent and v from ground to top, leaving out the faces of an arched door opening on the +x side so the tent is 'open'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: path, a, b, c, rings, segments, door

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Objects built from simple shapes (boxes, cylinders, capsules, spheres, ellipsoids) or our own meshes, for things Gazebo Fuel has no good model of and as offline fallbacks (--assets primitive): the open pop-up dome tent (the search target), debris (logs, plywood and roof sheets, lumber, tarps, tyres, bins, coolers, cartons, mattresses, pallets), bushes, corner poles, and fallback mannequin, person, sedan, pickup, canopy, cone, chair, table and barrel. Most return (parts, meta) with the size for the truth file.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by the generators and builder.py; colour palettes for tents, cars and clothes live here.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Picks a random (key, value) pair from a dict with the numpy random generator.
Makes a capsule part whose axis runs from point a to point b (used for the fallback mannequin's arms and legs).
The open pop-up dome tent (2.4 x 2.2 x 1.35 m, door at +x): the textured double-sided dome mesh, a dark elliptical floor seen through the door, the door flap lying in front, and one collision box.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: dome mesh URI, fabric picture URI, colour
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.outputs: (parts, meta with size 3.15 x 2.2 x 1.35 including the flap)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: A clothed dummy about 1.8 m tall made of boxes, spheres and capsules with random arm and leg angles, turned into one of five poses (lying face up, face down, on its side, sitting, standing), set on the ground, centred and given a collision box. Only used with --assets primitive (the default hiker is Rescue Randy).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: generator, pose, colours (shirt, pants, skin, hair)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: A standing person about 1.78 m tall with a hi-vis vest and stripe (fallback for the Fuel people).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: generator, vest, shirt, pants, skin, hair colours

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: A sedan car 4.7 x 1.8 x 1.42 m made of boxes and four wheels, front at +x (fallback vehicle).
A pickup truck 5.5 x 2.0 x 1.85 m with cab, bed and four wheels, front at +x (fallback vehicle).
A 3 x 3 m pop-up canopy: four poles and a flat roof with a peak (fallback for the Fuel canopy at the flight line).
A 0.7 m orange traffic cone with a black base and white band (fallback).
A folding camp chair: seat, tilted back and four legs (fallback).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Writes the SDF text of static objects from simple 'parts' (one shape with a colour, or one mesh file with an optional material), places objects in the world, and has small helpers for rotations (roll-pitch-yaw <-> 3x3 matrix, SDF's R = Rz x Ry x Rx) and bounding boxes so objects can be turned and set exactly on the ground.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: The lowest layer of worldgen: assets, primitives and builder all produce parts and call model_xml / include_xml from here.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Turns an SDF roll-pitch-yaw triple (radians) into a 3x3 rotation matrix R = Rz(yaw) x Ry(pitch) x Rx(roll).
Turns a rotation matrix back into roll, pitch, yaw (pitch between -90 and 90 degrees; in gimbal lock everything goes into yaw).
Formats a pose as the SDF text 'x y z roll pitch yaw' with 4 decimals.
Makes text safe inside an XML comment by replacing every '--' (forbidden there; strict parsers reject the file) and trailing dashes.

Describes one part as a dict: shape (box, cylinder, capsule, sphere, ellipsoid or mesh with URI, scale and sub-mesh), size, pose, colour, collision and visual switches, roughness, double-sided, shadows and optional material maps (material None keeps a mesh's own colours).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: name, shape, size, pose, colour, options

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: An invisible collision-only box: one cheap physics shape around an object made of many visuals.

Writes the <geometry> inner text of a part's shape (box size, cylinder or capsule radius and length, sphere radius, ellipsoid radii, or mesh URI with sub-mesh and scale); an unknown shape raises ValueError.
Writes a part's <material>: colour as ambient and diffuse, fixed specular, PBR maps (albedo, normal, roughness, metalness) and roughness; empty when the part keeps the mesh's own material.
Writes a part's <collision> (if wanted) and <visual> (unless hidden) with pose, shadows, geometry and material.
Writes a complete STATIC <model> holding all parts in one link, placed at xyz with heading yaw (or a full rpy), with an optional comment above it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: name, parts, xyz, yaw, rpy, comment

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes an <include> of a model by URI (model://... or a Fuel URL), forced static, at a pose.
Rotates every part about the object origin by a 3x3 matrix and then shifts it, updating both positions and orientations.
A few surface points of a simple-shape part in the object frame (box corners, cylinder/capsule rings, sphere and ellipsoid extremes; a mesh counts as one point), used for bounding boxes.
The lowest and highest corner (min_xyz, max_xyz) of a list of simple-shape parts.
Moves parts up or down so their lowest point sits exactly at z = clearance (on the ground).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: Paints every texture of the worlds with numpy and Pillow, so worlds rebuild anywhere without photos (same seed = same picture): the seamless 4096 x 4096 grass picture covering 160 x 160 m (3.9 cm per pixel, only weak big blotches so the repeat does not show), dry / lush / dirt patch cut-outs with dithered edges, tent nylon with pole seams and a darker skirt, the concrete pad with an H, the runway with markings and numbers 02/20, and the creek water with mud banks.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Called by builder.write_shared_models and build_suas_field.write_creek_model.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Makes seamless (tileable) fractal noise: white noise filtered by 1/f^beta in the frequency domain, normalised to mean 0 and spread 1. beta about 0.7 gives fine grain, 1.5 clouds, 2.5 soft blobs; max_wavelength_px removes waves longer than that so a repeated picture shows no big pattern.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: generator, size n x m, beta, max wavelength

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: 0 below lo, 1 above hi and a smooth S-curve in between (also works falling when lo > hi); used to turn noise into soft masks.
Turns a float RGB array with values 0..1 into an 8-bit Pillow image.
Saves a JPEG without colour subsampling (thin lines keep their colour).
Saves a PNG (keeps transparency).
Makes the small-scale grass structure shared by the ground and the patches: blade-scale grain, 5-30 cm tufts of darker weeds and scattered pale stalks.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: generator, height, width, max tuft wavelength

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Paints the seamless ground picture for a 160 x 160 m tile: olive September green mixed with straw-coloured dry grass by band-limited noise (1-10 m spots, a weak 8-30 m layer), darker tufts up to 5 m, pale stalks and fine grain.
Makes an irregular blob mask: fully opaque inside, transparent outside, with a randomly dithered rim (Gazebo draws cut-outs hard, so dithering looks like a soft edge from the air).
Paints one RGBA patch picture of 'dry' grass, 'lush' grass or bare 'dirt' with grass-like detail inside and a dithered blob edge; an unknown kind raises ValueError.

Paints the dome tent's nylon (u around the tent, v ground to top): panel colour with slight shading, the lowest 18 % in the darker skirt colour, four dark pole seams at 45/135/225/315 degrees narrowing towards the top, and a light window band near the top.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: generator, panel colour, accent colour, width, height

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns which of the 7 segments (a-g) light up for a digit 0-9.
Paints a 7-segment digit into a pixel box (used for the runway numbers).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: draw object, box, digit, colour, stroke

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Paints the asphalt strip (24 pixels per metre) with edge lines, a dashed centre line, threshold bars at both ends and the runway numbers '02' and '20'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: generator, length, width, pixels per metre, numbers

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Paints the square concrete take-off pad with a white circle, a big white H and a dark border.
Paints the creek strip across its width: grass, mud bank, dark water with streaks, mud bank, grass.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.explain: The parts of a world file that are the same for every world: the header (1 ms physics at real-time factor 1 for ArduPilot lock-step; systems Physics, UserCommands, SceneBroadcaster, Sensors with ogre2, Imu, NavSat; <spherical_coordinates> equal to SITL's --home; scene and a south-east September sun), the demo GUI (3D view, CameraTracking for /gui/follow, world control and stats, a floating 640 x 400 'Drone camera (live)' panel showing /sim/camera/video/image) and the closing tags.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/si.how_it_fits: Used by builder.world_sdf; the camera topic constant matches sim_models' contract.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Computes a GUI camera pose at 'eye' looking at 'target' (pitch positive = looking down, yaw towards the target).
Returns the gz-gui settings block for a small, fixed-size floating helper plugin without a title bar.

Writes the world's <gui> block: the 3D view with its starting camera, invisible helpers, CameraTracking with follow target 'iris', offset (-12, 0, 6) m and gain 0.02 (following starts only when the bringup calls /gui/follow), world control, world stats and the floating 'Drone camera (live)' ImageDisplay anchored top-right.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: camera pose, follow settings, camera topic, panel size

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Writes the start of a world file up to the sun: the PURPOSE comment, <world name>, the GUI, the 1 ms physics, the six systems, <spherical_coordinates> (EARTH_WGS84, ENU, the home latitude/longitude/elevation/heading = SITL's --home), the scene and the directional sun.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.inputs: world name, Home, purpose lines, GUI text

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/sim.explain: Returns the closing tags '</world></sdf>' of a world file.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/te.explain: Shared pytest setup of sim_worlds: puts the package source folder and its scripts/ folder on Python's import path (so the tests check THIS code whether installed or not) and offers a pkg_dir fixture with the package folder.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/te.how_it_fits: Loaded automatically by pytest before the sim_worlds tests.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/te.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_worlds (run by colcon test and test_sim_worlds.sh).

Unit tests of the QGC WPL 110 writer/reader and of the team-shape checks (sim_worlds.mission and planner), including the committed mission files; the index rules mirror waypoint_mavros/waypoint.py and main_controller.py.

Checks the real-terrain research fixes with small synthetic arrays, without raw GIS downloads or Gazebo: Sentinel-2 offsets and the grass-grade fallback, lidar haze and roof heights, tree confirmation and roof exclusion, building roofs, poles and the site pack's source credits.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/te.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_worlds (WIP real-terrain parts).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/tr.explain: The answer key of the runway world: home, class ids (person '0', tent '1'), the search box with its corners in metres and latitude/longitude, the targets (the hiker = Rescue Randy mannequin and the open pop-up tent) and every distractor, each with Gazebo name, x/y/z/yaw, latitude/longitude in ArduPilot's convention and exact WGS84, height, bounding box and distance from home. mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/tr.how_it_fits: Read by sim_demo's truth_detector (detector:=truth), demo_markers and score_run (location, aim and drop errors).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/tr.explain: The answer key of the suas_field world: the same fields as runway's for two search boundaries (one hiker and one tent each, plus vehicles, standing people, bushes and debris), plus counts, the 11-point flight boundary, the altitude rule 45.7-121.9 m above ground, the runways and the creek centre line. GENERATED by build_suas_field.py.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/tr.how_it_fits: Read by sim_demo for scoring and markers when the suas_field world runs.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/wo.explain: The Gazebo world 'runway' (about 3000 lines, GENERATED by build_runway.py): its own GUI layout with a 'Drone camera (live)' panel, 1 ms physics, the Physics, UserCommands, SceneBroadcaster, Sensors (ogre2), Imu and NavSat systems, spherical coordinates equal to SITL's home, the ground, pad, runway, a flight line, the 120 x 100 m search box with one hiker and one tent among distractors, trees and grass patches. The drone is not in it.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/wo.explain: The Gazebo world 'suas_field' (about 13,000 lines, GENERATED by build_suas_field.py): the SUAS 2026 site with origin at the VTOL pad (Runway 2), Runway 1, the flight boundary markers, two search boundaries each with one hiker and one open pop-up tent among debris, vehicles, bushes and standing people, a creek with trees in the north, plus the same systems and GUI as runway.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/CM.explain: Build rules (ament_cmake, nothing to compile). It installs the Python module sim_models, the two programs payload_release and generate_model_sdf into lib/sim_models, the folders models/, config/ and launch/, the test world and acceptance scripts, registers the environment hook that adds share/sim_models/models to GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH, and registers 5 pytest tests for colcon test.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/CM.how_it_fits: colcon build reads it; it is why 'ros2 run sim_models payload_release' works and why Gazebo finds model://iris_a8mini after sourcing the workspace.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/RE.explain: The full guide to the simulated drone: what is in the package, the model tree, gimbal sign conventions (yaw + = camera turns left, roll + = right side down, pitch -90 deg = straight down), every Gazebo topic and ROS parameter, how one payload drop flows from main_controller to the falling bottle, the SITL parameter table, how to regenerate model.sdf, the tests with the latest measured acceptance results, design notes and troubleshooting.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/RE.how_it_fits: Documentation; the interface tables here are the contract other packages code against.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/pa.explain: The ROS 2 package manifest of sim_models (ament_cmake + ament_cmake_python): description of the drone, maintainer astra-sim@example.com, run-time dependencies rclpy, std_msgs, launch, launch_ros, xacro, ament_index_python and ros_gz_sim. ArduPilot SITL, ardupilot_gazebo and pymavlink are installed by 02_setup_ardupilot.sh, not by rosdep.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/co.explain: Extra ArduCopter SITL parameters, loaded after ArduPilot's copter.parm and gazebo-iris.parm so they win: SERVO11_FUNCTION 0 and SERVO13_FUNCTION 0 (outputs free for MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO, like the team's Pixhawk; MIN/TRIM 500, MAX 1900), MNT1_TYPE 0 (ArduPilot does not drive the gimbal), AUTO_OPTIONS 3 (arm and take off in AUTO without RC sticks), FENCE_ENABLE 0, FS_GCS_ENABLE 0, PLND_ENABLED 0, battery failsafes warn only, SIM_SPEEDUP 1 (real time, because team code sleeps on the wall clock). Every line is under 90 characters because ArduPilot reads the file in 100-byte pieces.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/co.how_it_fits: sim_bringup's sim_paths.sitl_defaults puts it last in SITL's --defaults list; without it the team's drop commands would be refused ('Channel 11 is already in use'). test_astra_sitl_parm.py checks it.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/en.explain: A one-line environment hook: 'prepend-non-duplicate;GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH;share/sim_models/models'. When the workspace's setup file is sourced it puts the package's models folder in front of Gazebo's model search path.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/en.how_it_fits: Lets Gazebo find model://iris_a8mini (and its meshes) without any manual path setting.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/la.explain: A launch file that starts only the payload_release node, with its most useful parameters as launch arguments: open_threshold_us (1400.0), min_open_time_s (0.0), world_origin_lat/lon/alt (nan = unknown; set them to the world's spherical coordinates to get latitude/longitude in the events) and use_sim_time (false).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/la.how_it_fits: For running the drop mechanism by hand (ros2 launch sim_models payload_release.launch.py). sim.launch.py does not use it: it starts the node directly with default parameters.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/lau.explain: Declares the six launch arguments and one Node: package sim_models, executable payload_release, name payload_release, with the numbers converted to floats (and use_sim_time to a bool).
Turns a launch argument into a parameter value of type float (so '1400.0' or 'nan' arrive as numbers, not text).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.explain: The Gazebo model description: name iris_a8mini, version 1.0, model file model.sdf (SDF 1.9), author and a short description (Iris + A8 mini gimbal + live and photo cameras + water bottle on servo 11 and beacon on servo 13; needs model://iris_with_standoffs and the ArduPilotPlugin).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.how_it_fits: Gazebo reads it when anything asks for model://iris_a8mini.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.explain: The plain SDF of the drone, GENERATED from model.sdf.xacro with the default arguments (zr10 2560x1440 photos, ArduPilotPlugin on UDP 9002, both payloads) and committed, so model://iris_a8mini works without running xacro. Its header comment lists the arguments used. Do not edit it by hand.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.how_it_fits: Fallback used by sim_paths.generate_drone_sdf when xacro fails; test_model_generation.py checks it equals the xacro output. Regenerate with ros2 run sim_models generate_model_sdf --update-default.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.explain: The SOURCE file of the simulated drone, written in xacro (SDF with variables). It includes ardupilot_gazebo's iris_with_standoffs unchanged (body, legs, IMU, 4 rotors with the same aerodynamics) and adds a SIYI A8 mini gimbal 7 cm forward under the nose carrying two 81 deg cameras: live video 1280x720 at 25 Hz, and a TRIGGERED photo camera (2560x1440 for zr10, 3840x2160 for a8mini) that renders one picture per trigger message. It also adds two droppable payloads (0.5 kg water bottle 'person', 0.12 kg beacon 'tent') held by DetachableJoints, and the ArduPilotPlugin that links the model to SITL. The gimbal limits are yaw +-160, roll +-30 and pitch -135..+45 degrees, and it turns at about 90 deg/s.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.effects: Gazebo topics in: /sim/gimbal/{yaw,roll,pitch}/cmd_pos, /sim/camera/photo/trigger, /sim/payload/<name>/detach. Out: /sim/camera/video/image, /sim/camera/photo/image (+ camera_info), /sim/gimbal/joint_states (50 Hz), /sim/drone/odometry (50 Hz, world ENU), /sim/payload/servo11 and /servo13 (SITL outputs 11/13 in microseconds), /sim/payload/<name>/state and /odometry. UDP fdm_port_in (9002+10I) to SITL in lock-step; SITL outputs 1-4 spin the motors.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.how_it_fits: sim_bringup runs it through xacro at every start (camera profile and SITL port as arguments) and spawns it as 'iris'; generate_model_sdf.py makes the committed model.sdf from it. Every /sim/... Gazebo topic of the drone is defined here.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.explain: Says where the four gimbal meshes (a8_mini_base/yaw/roll/pitch.stl) come from: the siyi_ros2 project (github.com/mzahana/siyi_ros2), used unchanged, and reproduces its MIT license.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/mo.how_it_fits: Licence notice for the 3D shapes that make the gimbal look like a real A8 mini.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sc.explain: Command-line tool that turns model.sdf.xacro into a plain SDF with chosen options: --camera-model zr10|a8mini, photo/video size and rate, --hfov, --noise, --instance I or --fdm-port-in, --no-payloads, payload masses, initial gimbal pitch, -o FILE or --update-default (rewrite the committed model.sdf). Without -o it prints the SDF. Exit 0 written, 2 bad arguments, 1 xacro failed.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sc.how_it_fits: Installed as 'ros2 run sim_models generate_model_sdf'; used by developers and the acceptance test. sim_bringup does its own xacro call at launch.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/scr.explain: Defines and reads the command-line options (camera profile, photo and video sizes, fps, field of view, noise, SITL instance or port, payload switch and masses, initial gimbal pitch, xacro file, output file or --update-default), with defaults taken from model_generator.DEFAULT_ARGS.

Collects the options into model arguments, refuses --update-default unless every argument is at its default, calls model_generator.generate_model_sdf, and writes the result to the -o file, to model.sdf next to the xacro (--update-default) or to the screen.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sc.explain: The tiny program behind 'ros2 run sim_models payload_release': it only imports and calls main() of sim_models/payload_release_node.py, where all the logic lives.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sc.how_it_fits: Installed as lib/sim_models/payload_release by CMakeLists.txt; sim.launch.py starts it when payload:=true.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.explain: Marks sim_models as a Python package and describes its two helper modules: payload_logic (when to drop, when landed, ENU to latitude/longitude) and model_generator (xacro to SDF).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.how_it_fits: Lets the scripts write 'from sim_models.payload_release_node import main'.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.explain: Turns model.sdf.xacro into an SDF text with checked arguments. It knows the camera profiles (zr10 2560x1440, a8mini 3840x2160), the defaults of every xacro argument, the SITL port rule 9002 + 10 x instance, validates every value (sizes, fov below pi, ports 1024-65535, masses, pitch limits -2.3562..0.7854 rad), runs xacro and replaces the source comments with a 'GENERATED FILE' header listing the arguments.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.how_it_fits: Used by scripts/generate_model_sdf.py and the tests; sim_bringup's launch has its own simpler xacro call (sim_paths.generate_drone_sdf).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: Returns the UDP port the drone's ArduPilotPlugin must listen on for SITL instance I: 9002 + 10 x I. A negative instance raises ValueError.
Returns the photo size of a camera profile: zr10 = (2560, 1440), a8mini = (3840, 2160). Any other name raises ValueError listing the known ones.
Finds model.sdf.xacro: first in the installed package (share/sim_models/models/iris_a8mini/), else in the source tree next to this file, so tools and tests also work before colcon build.
Converts a value to a whole number and checks it is not negative; otherwise raises ValueError naming the argument.
Converts a value to a decimal number and checks it is above 0 (or at least 0 when allow_zero); otherwise raises ValueError naming the argument.

Checks the model arguments and returns them as xacro text values. Unknown keys are refused; missing ones take the defaults; 'instance' sets fdm_port_in = 9002 + 10 x instance; photo width and height must be given together (0 = from the profile); video sizes and fps must be above 0; hfov must be below pi; the port must be 1024-65535; payloads must be true/false; masses positive; gimbal_initial_pitch inside -2.3562..0.7854 rad.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.effects: raises ValueError with a plain message on a bad value

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: Returns the photo size the camera will really get for these arguments: the explicit photo_width/photo_height when both are above 0, else the camera profile's size.

Writes the text of the comment put at the top of a generated model.sdf: 'GENERATED FILE, do not edit', what the model is, where the source is, how to regenerate, the photo size, the ArduPilotPlugin port and all arguments wrapped to 88 characters (with no double hyphens, which XML comments forbid).

Runs xacro on model.sdf.xacro with the checked arguments and returns the SDF text. It removes the source file's leading comments and the orphan comments xacro leaves under <sdf>, adds the generated-file header, and puts one note in front of <model> explaining why canonical_link must stay the Iris body.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.effects: raises ValueError for bad arguments, ImportError when xacro is missing

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.explain: The decisions behind the simulated payload drop, as plain Python (no ROS, no Gazebo) so they are unit-tested anywhere: ServoReleaseDetector says 'drop now' exactly once, the first time the release servo reads OPEN (at or above 1400 us, the team's open value); LandingDetector says when the falling payload has stopped moving; enu_to_geodetic turns Gazebo east/north/up metres into latitude/longitude/altitude.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.how_it_fits: Used by payload_release_node.py. The rule 'first reading >= threshold' (not 'a jump from closed to open') is on purpose: a node started late may see 1400 as its first value and must still drop.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: Decides when ONE payload must be released from its servo's pulse width. It remembers whether it already released, when, with which pulse width, and the last value seen; an optional minimum open time can ignore glitches.

Stores the open threshold (default 1400 us) and the minimum open time (default 0 s = drop on the first open reading) and starts in the 'not released' state. A threshold that is not positive or a negative time raises ValueError.
Returns True when a pulse width means OPEN: at least the threshold minus 0.5 us (the relayed value can arrive as 1399.9999). None, NaN, 0, 500 and 1000 all count as closed.

Feeds one servo reading. It returns True exactly once: on the reading that decides the release (open, and open long enough if a minimum time is set). Closed readings reset the open timer; after the release it always returns False.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.inputs: pulse width (us), time of the reading (s)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: Decides when a dropped payload has come to rest, from its world positions after the release: it must move slower than rest_speed (0.05 m/s) for rest_time_s (1 s), and the first 0.3 s of the fall are ignored. It keeps the start point and the landed point.
Stores the rest speed, rest time and minimum fall time (raising ValueError for impossible values) and starts with no start or landing point.
True once start() was called (the payload was released).
True once the payload has come to rest.
Remembers the release time and position (world metres) and clears any earlier landing.

Feeds one position sample. It computes the speed since the previous sample; once the payload has been slower than the rest speed for the rest time (and the first 0.3 s of the fall are over) it records the landed point and returns True, exactly once.
After the landing returns how long the fall took, how far it fell and how far it drifted sideways from the release point, rounded to millimetres; an empty dict before that.

Converts a Gazebo position in metres (x east, y north, z up) to latitude, longitude and altitude, given the world origin (the world's <spherical_coordinates>). It uses the WGS-84 ellipsoid's local curvature radii, accurate to millimetres over a SUAS field.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.inputs: east, north, up, origin lat, lon, alt

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.explain: The drone's 'release mechanism' as a ROS 2 node 'payload_release'. It reads the Gazebo servo topics /sim/payload/servo11 and /servo13 directly with the gz-transport Python bindings (throttled from 1000 to 50 messages per second), and when a servo reaches 1400 us (main_controller's DO_SET_SERVO open value) it publishes on /sim/payload/<name>/detach so the DetachableJoint lets that payload fall. It confirms the detachment, watches /sim/payload/<name>/odometry until the payload lands, and publishes JSON events released / detached / landed / attached on the ROS topic /sim/payload/events.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.how_it_fits: Started by sim.launch.py (payload:=true). It is the link between the team's drop command (MAVROS -> SITL servo output) and a visible drop in Gazebo; the decisions are in payload_logic, the Gazebo side is hidden in GzLink so tests can use a fake.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/si.effects: publishes gz /sim/payload/<name>/detach and ROS /sim/payload/events; logs every servo change, release and landing

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: A thin wrapper around Gazebo's Python transport library (gz.transport13 / gz.msgs10) that hands plain Python values to callbacks: Double -> float, Odometry -> (sim time, x, y, z), StringMsg -> text, and can publish Empty messages.

Imports the Gazebo message types (Double, Empty, Odometry, StringMsg) and creates a gz-transport node. Raises ImportError when the bindings (python3-gz-transport13, python3-gz-msgs10) are missing, which main() turns into a clear message.
Makes gz-transport subscription options; when a rate is given it sets msgs_per_sec so Gazebo drops extra messages before Python sees them.
Subscribes to a Gazebo topic of gz.msgs.Double (here the servo pulse widths) and calls the callback with the number, at most rate_hz times per second.
Subscribes to a Gazebo odometry topic (drone or payload position) and calls the callback with (simulation time in seconds, x, y, z), at most rate_hz per second.
Turns one gz.msgs.Odometry message into (time from the header stamp, or NaN without a header, x, y, z) and passes it to the callback.
Subscribes to a Gazebo text topic (the DetachableJoint state 'attached' / 'detached') and calls the callback with the text.
Opens a Gazebo publisher for gz.msgs.Empty on a topic (here /sim/payload/<name>/detach) and returns a small function that sends one empty message each time it is called; None if advertising failed.

Everything the node tracks for ONE payload: its name, servo number, Gazebo topics, its release and landing detectors, the detach publisher, how many detach messages were sent, the last state text and position, and three thread-safe inboxes where Gazebo's background threads drop new values.
Stores the payload's name, servo, topics, ServoReleaseDetector and LandingDetector, and sets up empty inboxes protected by a lock.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.inputs: name, servo, topics dict, detector, landing detector

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: Called from a Gazebo thread with a new servo value: puts (current monotonic time, value) into the servo inbox.
Called from a Gazebo thread with a new payload position: puts it into the odometry inbox.
Called from a Gazebo thread with the DetachableJoint's state text: puts it into the state inbox.
Returns everything collected since the last call (servo samples, positions, state texts) and empties the inboxes, under the lock.
Builds the ROS node class only when it is needed (importing rclpy inside), so the module can be imported and tested without ROS. Returns rclpy and the PayloadReleaseNode class.

The ROS 2 node 'payload_release'. Parameters: payloads ['person', 'tent'], <name>.servo (11 person, 13 tent) and its four Gazebo topics, open_threshold_us 1400, min_open_time_s 0, servo_sample_rate_hz 50, drone_odometry_topic /sim/drone/odometry, events_topic /sim/payload/events, landing_rest_speed 0.05 m/s, landing_rest_time_s 1 s, world_origin_lat/lon/alt (NaN = unknown) and detach_repeats 3.

Creates the node, declares and reads the parameters, opens the /sim/payload/events publisher (reliable, transient local, depth 20, so late listeners still get the events), builds one PayloadChannel per payload, connects to Gazebo (a real GzLink, or the fake a test passes) and starts a 50 Hz timer. It logs which servo and topics each payload uses.

Declares the node's general parameters with their defaults: payloads, open_threshold_us (1400), min_open_time_s, servo_sample_rate_hz (50), drone_odometry_topic, events_topic, landing_rest_speed, landing_rest_time_s, world_origin_lat/lon/alt (NaN) and detach_repeats (3).

For each payload name declares <name>.servo (default 11 for person, 13 for tent) and its servo, detach, odometry and state topic parameters (defaults /sim/payload/servo<N>, /sim/payload/<name>/detach, /odometry, /state), and makes a PayloadChannel with fresh detectors. A payload without a servo number is skipped with an error.

Subscribes to the drone odometry (10 per second) and, for every payload, to its servo topic (throttled to servo_sample_rate_hz), its odometry (20 per second) and its state topic, and opens its detach publisher. Anything that fails to connect is logged.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.effects: gz subscriptions and one gz publisher per payload

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: Stores the newest drone position (t, x, y, z) under a lock; it is logged and reported at a release.

The 50 Hz main loop. For each payload it empties the inboxes, feeds positions to the landing detector (calling _on_landed when it lands), feeds servo values to the release detector (logging changes and calling _release on the deciding reading), handles state texts, and resends the detach if needed.
Logs a line such as 'servo 11 (person): 1000 us -> 1400 us (OPEN)' whenever the rounded servo value changes.

Drops one payload: starts the landing detector at the payload's last position (or the drone's, with a warning when the payload has no odometry yet), sends the detach message, logs 'RELEASE payload ...' with the servo value and drone position, and publishes a 'released' event.
Publishes one empty message on the payload's Gazebo detach topic and counts it; if there is no publisher it logs an error once.
After a release, resends the detach every 0.2 s until the joint reports 'detached' or detach_repeats (3) messages were sent, in case the first message was lost.

Handles a new DetachableJoint state text. 'detached' logs that the payload is falling and publishes a 'detached' event. 'attached' after a release means a new payload is held again (Gazebo restarted or the drone was re-spawned): it resets the detectors so the new payload can be dropped and publishes 'attached'. Anything else after a release is logged as a warning.

Logs where the payload came to rest (east/north/up, plus latitude/longitude when the world origin is set), how far and how long it fell and its drift, and publishes a 'landed' event with those numbers.
Converts a world position to latitude/longitude/altitude with enu_to_geodetic, or returns None while the world origin parameters are NaN.
Formats a position for the log as 'E x N y U z m' plus '(lat ... lon ...)' when known, or 'unknown position'.

Publishes one JSON line on /sim/payload/events: event name, payload, servo, wall time, the payload position (for 'released' the release point) and the drone position as position_enu / drone_enu, their simulation times, latitude/longitude/altitude when the world origin is known, plus any extra numbers (pwm_us, fall_time_s, fall_height_m, drift_m).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.inputs: event name, channel, optional position, drone position, extra fields

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/sim.explain: Entry point of 'ros2 run sim_models payload_release': builds the node class, starts ROS, runs the node until Ctrl+C and returns 0. If the Gazebo Python bindings are missing it prints how to install them and returns 1.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.explain: Checks config/astra_sitl.parm the way ArduPilot reads it: it re-creates ArduPilot's 100-byte line reader, checks every line is under 90 characters and commented, names are at most 16 characters, and the values the simulation needs are there (SERVO11/13_FUNCTION 0, MNT1_TYPE 0, AUTO_OPTIONS 3, FENCE_ENABLE 0, SIM_SPEEDUP 1).

Unit tests of the acceptance test's camera geometry on the REAL generated model: pitch -90 deg looks straight down with the picture top toward the nose, yaw + turns the camera left, roll + puts the right side down, a point straight ahead lands in the image centre.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.how_it_fits: pytest / colcon test of sim_models (needs xacro).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.explain: Checks that model.sdf.xacro produces the contracted drone for both camera profiles: names, joints and limits, every /sim/... topic, camera settings (resolution, 25 Hz, 81 deg, triggered photo), ArduPilotPlugin port and channels (motors 0-3, COMMAND channels 10/12 for servos 11/13), payload wiring and placement, argument checking, and that the committed model.sdf equals the default xacro output.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.how_it_fits: pytest / colcon test of sim_models (needs xacro; runs 'gz sdf -k' when Gazebo is found).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.explain: Unit tests of payload_logic without ROS or Gazebo: the team's 1400 us open / 500 us closed sequence releases exactly once, closed values never release, landing detection, fall summary and the ENU to latitude/longitude conversion.

Tests the payload_release ROS node without Gazebo: a fake GzLink records subscriptions and lets the test inject servo values, positions and joint states while _tick is called by hand. Checks no drop while closed, exactly one release at 1400 us, detach repeats until confirmed, the released / detached / landed events, and that the other payload is untouched.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.how_it_fits: pytest / colcon test of sim_models (needs rclpy).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.explain: The flight acceptance test driver: with Gazebo, the drone, payload_release and SITL already started by run_acceptance.sh, it measures over MAVLink (pymavlink, tcp 5760+10I) and gz-transport whether the model keeps its promises: parameters loaded, arm, take-off to 15 m and 20 s hover, 30 m cruise with payloads, gimbal slew and camera direction (coloured targets where the geometry predicts), one photo per trigger, real-time factor, both payload drops, landing. Results go to results.json and summary.txt.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.how_it_fits: Heavy test run by hand (not in the pytest suite); its latest numbers are in the README.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.explain: Answers 'where SHOULD this world point appear in the gimbal camera picture?': GimbalKinematics computes the camera pose from the drone pose and the three joint angles (offsets read from the generated SDF), PinholeCamera projects points like Gazebo's ideal camera, and find_blob finds the centre of one bright colour in a picture. Only numpy is needed.

Starts everything the flight acceptance test needs, headless: Gazebo with test/worlds/sim_models_test.sdf, the drone generated for the chosen SITL instance (default 1) and spawned as 'iris', payload_release, and ArduCopter SITL with copter.parm, gazebo-iris.parm and astra_sitl.parm; then runs acceptance_driver.py and stops only what it started. Options --instance, --camera-model, --out, --tests, --keep. Exit 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 setup problem.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.how_it_fits: Heavy manual test of sim_models (uses its own GZ_PARTITION sim_models_test and ROS_DOMAIN_ID 41).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_models/te.explain: The small test world of the acceptance test: ardupilot_gazebo iris_runway settings (1 ms physics, CMAC airfield) plus brightly coloured targets at known places (2 m squares 5 m north/east/south/west of the spawn point, 30 m poles 60 m away) and a fixed inspection camera that photographs the drone. The drone itself is spawned by the test.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/R.explain: The package guide in plain words: what sim.launch.py starts and in which order, every launch argument with its default, what team_stack.launch.py adds, the ports/topics/files table and the helper commands (ros2 run sim_bringup <name>).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/R.how_it_fits: Documentation only; the full simulator guide is simulation/README.md.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/p.explain: The ROS 2 package manifest of sim_bringup (ament_python): name, version 0.1.0, maintainer astra-sim@example.com and the run-time dependencies (rclpy, launch, ros_gz_sim, ros_gz_bridge, rviz2, xacro, mavros_msgs, tf2_ros, python3-yaml ...). The other simulation packages are deliberately NOT listed, so sim_bringup still builds when one of them is broken.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/p.how_it_fits: colcon reads it to know how to build and install the package; rosdep reads it to install the dependencies.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: Tells Python's setuptools to put the package's command-line programs into lib/sim_bringup, the folder where 'ros2 run sim_bringup <name>' looks for them.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: Standard file of every ament_python package; without it ros2 run would not find mission_tool, phase_monitor and the others.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: The build and install recipe of sim_bringup. It installs the Python modules, the two launch files, rviz/sim.rviz, everything in config/ (the Gazebo window layouts gazebo_gui.config, gazebo_gui_no_camera.config and gazebo_camera_window.config) and the README, and creates the 7 commands wait_then_exec, gz_follow, odom_tf, mission_tool, phase_monitor, stack_check and photo_trigger (each one points at the main() of its module).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: colcon build runs it (03_build.sh does that); it is why 'ros2 run sim_bringup mission_tool' works.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/c.explain: The layout of the Gazebo window (1500x900, dark theme). It has a big 3D view (MinimalScene, ogre2), the invisible helpers (scene manager, mouse view control, CameraTracking which provides the /gui/follow service, markers, entity selection and right-click menu), a floating 'Camera POV (live)' ImageDisplay that shows the Gazebo topic /sim/camera/video/image, and the play/pause and real-time-factor boxes.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/c.how_it_fits: With the default gui_camera:=panel, sim.launch.py passes it to 'gz sim -g --gui-config' when the world has no <gui> section of its own (or gui_config:=astra); gui_camera:=window or off use gazebo_gui_no_camera.config (this layout minus the camera panel) instead. gz_follow needs the CameraTracking plugin from it. With the stand-in drone the launch writes a copy with the camera topic replaced.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/l.explain: The launch file that starts the whole simulator with one command (ros2 launch sim_bringup sim.launch.py). It declares 57 launch arguments (world, camera_model, gui, gui_camera, gui_env, rviz, panel, pov_server, detector, sitl_instance, ports, windows_gcs, emulator, payload, bridge, follow, plug-in profile ...) and then, in order, starts the Gazebo server and window (with gui_camera:=window the live camera gets its own small Gazebo window), spawns the drone 'iris', starts ArduCopter SITL and MAVProxy behind wait_then_exec, the SIYI camera emulator, payload_release, the ROS bridge + odom_tf, the sim_demo nodes, the Mission Planner camera stream (pov_server), RViz and gz_follow. A missing simulator package never crashes it: it prints a note and uses a stand-in or skips that part.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/l.how_it_fits: It is the simulator half of a run (the team code half is ./launcher.sh sim with team_stack.launch.py). demo.sh and start_sim.sh call it; it writes ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml so status.sh, demo.sh and START OVER know what is running.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/l.effects: starts processes gz sim (server, window and, with gui_camera:=window, a camera-only window), arducopter, mavproxy.py, siyi_emulator, payload_release, parameter_bridge, odom_tf, demo nodes, pov_server, rviz2, gz_follow; writes ~/.astra_sim/generated/* and ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml; sets GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH, GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH and GZ_VERSION=harmonic, and when they are not already set GZ_PARTITION=astra_sim, ASTRA_SIM_SESSION and (inside WSL) QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.explain: Asks ROS where a package's installed 'share' folder is (for example sim_models or sim_worlds) and returns that path. If the package is not built or not sourced it returns None instead of crashing, so the launch can print a friendly note and carry on.

Builds the path <package prefix>/lib/<package>/<name> of an installed command (for example sim_bringup/wait_then_exec or siyi_emulator/siyi_emulator) and returns it only when that file exists and may be run. Otherwise it returns None, which the launch uses to skip the part with a message.

Makes a launch action that puts some folders in FRONT of an environment variable's current list (folders separated by ':'), dropping empty entries and duplicates. sim.launch.py uses it for GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH (where Gazebo finds model:// folders and worlds) and GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH (where it finds libArduPilotPlugin.so).

Returns the extra environment for the window programs (Gazebo GUI, RViz, demo panel). If the user already set QT_QPA_PLATFORM (tests use 'offscreen') that value is kept; inside WSL2 it sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb because Qt windows, especially RViz's 3D view, are more reliable on X11 than on Wayland there. Elsewhere it returns an empty dict.
Reads /proc/version and returns True when the Linux kernel's version text mentions 'microsoft', which means the simulator runs inside Windows' WSL2. Returns False if the file cannot be read.

The heart of the launch file, run once when the launch starts. It reads every argument (and an optional plug-in profile), checks the numbers, picks the world (sim_paths.load_world_config, or the ardupilot_gazebo stand-in), refuses to start when SITL's ports 9002+10I / 5760+10I are already taken, and makes the drone SDF with xacro. Then it builds, in order, the list of programs and nodes to start (see effects), and last it writes state/current_launch.yaml.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.called_when: by the OpaqueFunction that generate_launch_description adds, after the launch arguments are known
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.outputs: the list of launch actions (processes, nodes, log lines, environment settings)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.effects: starts the gz sim server (its exit stops everything) and the Gazebo window (layout: the world's own <gui>, config/gazebo_gui.config, or with gui_camera:=window/off config/gazebo_gui_no_camera.config; gui_env NAME=value extras for the window only), plus with gui_camera:=window a second small Gazebo window that shows only the live camera (config/gazebo_camera_window.config); the spawn of entity 'iris', SITL (waits for UDP 9002+10I), MAVProxy (waits for TCP 5760+10I), siyi_emulator (camera_model, camera_ip, SD card ~/.astra_sim/sd_card_I<I>), payload_release, parameter_bridge + odom_tf, sim_demo's demo_nodes.launch.py, pov_server (port 8081), RViz and gz_follow; writes ~/.astra_sim/generated/ (drone SDF, bridge_I<I>.yaml) and ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml; may emit Shutdown on a fatal error

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.explain: Adds a log line that starts with '[sim] ' to the action list, so the message is printed in the launch terminal when the launch runs.
Adds an '[sim] ERROR: ...' log line plus a Shutdown event to the action list and returns the list, so the launch prints the reason and stops cleanly instead of showing a Python traceback.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.outputs: the action list (returned by _launch_setup as is)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.explain: Step 7: adds MAVProxy, the program that copies the autopilot's MAVLink to several listeners. It finds mavproxy.py, asks sim_paths.windows_gcs_output for the extra Windows copy, and builds the command: --master tcp:127.0.0.1:5760+10I (or mavlink_master), --out udp:127.0.0.1:14550 (scripts / ground station), --out udp:127.0.0.1:14552 (the MAVROS output; demo.sh and start_sim.sh now connect MAVROS straight to SITL SERIAL2 on TCP 5763+10I, so this is only the fallback door), --out udp:127.0.0.1:14553 (demo panel), any extra outputs, the Windows output, --daemon, the SITL run folder as state folder (~/.astra_sim/sitl_I<I> by default) and log mav.tlog. The command is started behind the given wait_then_exec words.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.inputs: waiter_prefix: the wait_then_exec words (empty = start at once)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.effects: adds the 'mavproxy' process; logs the chosen outputs; if MAVProxy is missing it only prints how to connect to TCP 5760 directly

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.explain: Tries to open a UDP socket on the given address. If that works the address belongs to this computer and it returns True. The launch uses it to warn when the camera address 192.168.144.25 is missing (then the team's video_cam cannot reach the camera emulator).

Writes ~/.astra_sim/state/current_launch.yaml: a comment line plus everything this launch decided (world, home, spawn, mission, truth, model file, camera, detector, SITL instance and ports, MAVProxy ports, Windows output, camera IP, photo folder, profile, GZ_PARTITION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID). If writing fails it only adds a log line.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.inputs: state folder, the info dict, the action list

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.explain: The function 'ros2 launch' calls. It declares every launch argument from the ARGUMENTS table with its default and help text. When they are not already set, it gives all started programs a session tag ASTRA_SIM_SESSION=launch-<12 hex> (stop_sim.sh uses it), sets GZ_PARTITION=astra_sim so other Gazebo programs do not mix in, and sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb inside WSL. Finally it adds _launch_setup to build everything else.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.called_when: ros2 launch sim_bringup sim.launch.py (from start_sim.sh / demo.sh)

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/l.explain: Runs the team's own mission stack, main/launch/tracker.launch.xml, unchanged, and only adds global parameters that the team's detector new_od declares: model_path (default ~/.astra_sim/models/yolo26m.pt, because the team default is a Jetson-only path), use_batched_inference false (the batched path only works with the Jetson's TensorRT .engine) and, in detector:=truth mode, camera_feed_path pointing at an always-empty folder. Arguments: detector real|truth|custom, mission_brain team|custom, model_path, batched, debug, profile.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/l.how_it_fits: ./launcher.sh sim runs it when TRACKER_CMD='ros2 launch sim_bringup team_stack.launch.py detector:=real' (demo.sh sets that). It starts the six team nodes (waypoint_manager, gps node, trigger, siyi, new_od, main_controller) exactly like on the Jetson; a plug-in profile can replace new_od or main_controller with a teammate's node.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/l.effects: starts the team nodes from tracker.launch.xml; may write a filtered copy of tracker.launch.xml into ~/.astra_sim/generated

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.explain: Returns the folder ~/.astra_sim/truth_mode_empty_feed and creates it if needed. In detector:=truth mode new_od is told to watch this always-empty folder, so it never detects anything and sim_demo's truth_detector is the only one publishing /image_detection.
Returns two launch actions: a '[team_stack] ERROR: ...' log line and a Shutdown event, so this launch stops with a clear reason (launcher.sh then stops MAVROS too and demo.sh reports it).

Resolves the arguments and builds the include of the team's tracker.launch.xml. It applies an optional plug-in profile, checks detector (real/truth/custom) and mission_brain (team/custom), finds main/launch/tracker.launch.xml, and sets the global parameters model_path (only if the weights file exists, otherwise a warning that new_od will detect nothing), use_batched_inference=false (unless batched:=true) and camera_feed_path (truth mode). For a custom detector or brain it uses sim_plugins.tracker_filter to make a copy of tracker.launch.xml without new_od or main_controller.py. The parameters are wrapped with the include in a scoped GroupAction so they reach only the tracker's nodes.

Entry point of 'ros2 launch sim_bringup team_stack.launch.py' (and of ./launcher.sh sim through TRACKER_CMD). Declares the arguments detector (default real), mission_brain (team), model_path (sim_paths.detector_model_path()), batched (false), debug (false) and profile (empty), then hands over to _setup.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/r.explain: An empty marker file. Installing it into share/ament_index/resource_index/packages is how ROS 2 learns that a package called sim_bringup exists.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/r.how_it_fits: Needed by ament_index (get_package_share_directory('sim_bringup')), which sim.launch.py uses to find its own RViz and Gazebo layouts.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/r.explain: The RViz window layout: a 10 m grid, the demo markers (/sim/demo/markers from sim_demo demo_markers: search area, true targets, detections, photo footprints, track), the drone TF frame, the drone odometry (/sim/drone/odometry), a big live camera picture (/sim/camera/image) and the newest photo (/sim/camera/photo). Fixed frame is 'world' (Gazebo world: x east, y north, z up, origin = SITL home); the 3D view follows 'base_link'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/r.how_it_fits: Opened by sim.launch.py when rviz:=true. The dock layout blob at the bottom is generated by test/gen_rviz_window_state.py.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: Marks the folder as the Python package sim_bringup, lists its modules in its comment and sets __version__ = '0.1.0'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: Lets other code write 'from sim_bringup import sim_paths'.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: Makes the Gazebo window's 3D view follow the drone like a chase camera. It waits until the window offers the service /gui/follow (from the CameraTracking plugin) and the entity 'iris' exists, then asks the GUI to follow it and sets the camera offset (default 12 m behind, 6 m above), all through the 'gz service' / 'gz model' command line tools. Exit 0 = following, 1 = gave up.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: Started by sim.launch.py when gui:=true and follow:=true (and by START OVER); it only changes the view, never the simulation.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Runs the Gazebo command line tool 'gz' with the given words and returns what it printed, or None when it failed, could not start or took longer than the timeout (15 s by default). It inherits GZ_PARTITION, so it talks to the same Gazebo as the simulator.
Runs 'gz service --list' and returns True when the given service name (here /gui/follow) is one of the lines, which means the Gazebo window is open.
Runs 'gz model --list' and returns True when a model with the given name (here 'iris') appears, which means the drone has been spawned.
Calls one Gazebo service once with 'gz service -s ... --timeout 3000' and returns True when the answer contains 'data: true'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: service, request type, reply type, request text

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Asks the Gazebo window to follow the entity (service /gui/follow with gz.msgs.StringMsg) and, if that worked, places the camera at the x, y, z offset in metres (service /gui/follow/offset with gz.msgs.Vector3d).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: True when the follow request was accepted

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Reads --entity (iris), --offset (-12 0 6) and --timeout (240 s), then loops every 2 s through three stages: wait for the window, wait for the drone, send the follow request. It prints progress every 20 s, returns 0 when following, and 1 with a hint (right-click the drone -> Follow) when it gives up.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: ros2 run sim_bringup gz_follow (sim.launch.py, START OVER)

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: A tiny MAVLink 'ground station' for the simulator built on pymavlink: it does what the pilot does in Mission Planner at the field. Subcommands: upload (a QGC WPL 110 .waypoints file), wait-ready (3D GPS fix, healthy EKF, pre-arm checks, booted 30 s), arm (GUIDED + arm with retries), start (MAV_CMD_MISSION_START -> AUTO), fly (all of these + take-off check), watch, status, mode NAME, rtl, land, disarm and check-mission (only checks the file).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: It connects to MAVProxy's ground-station output udpin:127.0.0.1:14550 as MAVLink system 245. The team code never arms or starts a mission, so demo.sh, fly_mission.sh, upload_mission.sh, status.sh, container_sim.sh and START OVER use this tool for those pilot steps. Exit codes 0 done, 1 failed, 2 bad usage.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Prints one message with the prefix '[mission] ' and flushes it, so it shows up at once in logs.

One line of a QGC WPL 110 mission file: seq, current, frame (0 global, 3 relative altitude, 2 mission), command number (MAV_CMD, e.g. 16 WAYPOINT, 22 TAKEOFF, 203 DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL, 20 RETURN_TO_LAUNCH), parameters p1-p4, x/y (latitude/longitude for location commands, otherwise parameters 5/6), z (altitude in m) and autocontinue.
The readable command name of the item, for example 'TAKEOFF' or 'DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL'; unknown numbers become 'CMD_<number>'.

x as the whole number MISSION_ITEM_INT needs: latitude x 10,000,000 for location commands (WAYPOINT, TAKEOFF, LAND ...), otherwise just the rounded value (for example DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL's shoot flag must not be scaled).
y as the whole number MISSION_ITEM_INT needs: longitude x 10,000,000 for location commands, otherwise the rounded plain value.

Reads a QGC WPL 110 mission text (the Mission Planner format) into MissionItems. The first line must start with 'QGC WPL', every other line needs 12 numbers (tabs, spaces or commas), and items are renumbered 0..N-1 in file order (item 0 = home). Raises ValueError with the line number for a broken file.

Checks a mission against what the team's code needs and summarises it: the index of the TAKEOFF (22), DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL (203, starts the 1 Hz photos) and RETURN_TO_LAUNCH (20, must be last), and how many WAYPOINTs come after the photo start (at least 2: photos stop at the second-to-last, the detector hold is at the last). Every problem becomes a warning sentence.
Returns the sequence number of the first item with the given command, or -1 when the mission has none.

A pymavlink connection to the simulated drone plus the little state the tool needs: the newest message of each type, collected STATUSTEXT lines, the autopilot's system/component id, and helpers for armed, mode, altitude, commands and mode switches.

Opens the MAVLink connection (default udpin:127.0.0.1:14550, our system id 245, component 190, ardupilotmega dialect) and waits up to the timeout for an ArduPilot heartbeat; then remembers the autopilot's system and component id. Raises RuntimeError with a hint when no heartbeat comes.
Reads HEARTBEAT messages for up to the timeout and returns the first one sent by an ArduPilot autopilot (ignoring heartbeats of ground stations or MAVROS). Returns None if none arrives.

Reads incoming MAVLink for the given seconds (at least once): it keeps the newest message of each type from the autopilot, collects STATUSTEXT texts, and returns early with the first message whose type is in 'types' if that list is given.
True when the newest heartbeat has the 'safety armed' bit set, which means the motors are armed.
The current flight mode name (GUIDED, AUTO, RTL ...) from the newest heartbeat's custom_mode number, using pymavlink's ArduCopter mode table; '?' before any heartbeat.
Height above home in metres from the newest GLOBAL_POSITION_INT message (relative_alt is in millimetres), or None before one arrived.
Returns the STATUSTEXT lines collected since the last call and empties the list.

Sends one COMMAND_LONG with the command number and up to 7 parameters (missing ones are 0) and waits up to 'wait' seconds for the COMMAND_ACK of that command addressed to us. Returns the ACK's result number, or None when no answer came.

Switches the flight mode by name (GUIDED, AUTO, RTL, LAND, LOITER ...): it repeats the mode request and listens 1 s each time until the heartbeat shows the new mode or 8 s pass. Unknown names are refused with the list of known ones.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: True when the mode is confirmed

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Uploads a mission with the MAVLink mission protocol: it sends MISSION_COUNT (repeated up to 3 times if the autopilot stays silent), then answers each MISSION_REQUEST_INT / MISSION_REQUEST with a MISSION_ITEM_INT (exact coordinates, latitude/longitude x 1e7 for location commands), skipping requests meant for another ground station. It succeeds when MISSION_ACK 'accepted' arrives after all items; any other ACK or a 30 s silence fails.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.effects: replaces the mission stored in ArduCopter SITL

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Waits until the drone could be armed: GPS_RAW_INT fix type 3 or better, EKF_STATUS_REPORT with attitude, horizontal velocity and absolute position flags, the autopilot booted at least 30 s, and (when reported) SYS_STATUS's pre-arm check bit healthy. Every 10 s it prints what is still missing plus the autopilot's last PreArm message; the default limit is 240 s.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: demo.sh before uploading (the first ~30-60 s of 'Arm: Gyros inconsistent' are normal)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Switches to GUIDED and sends the arm command (MAV_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM 1); it waits for the heartbeat to show 'armed', and while the autopilot refuses it prints the reason and tries again every 5 s, up to 120 s.

Sends MAV_CMD_MISSION_START so ArduCopter switches to AUTO and flies the mission from the first item (a plain AUTO switch on the ground would wait for the pilot's throttle). If that is refused it falls back to a normal AUTO mode switch.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: True when the drone is in AUTO

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Waits up to 45 s until the drone is at least 2 m above home (GLOBAL_POSITION_INT relative altitude) and then prints 'TAKEOFF confirmed'. It fails early when the drone disarms instead of taking off.

Prints every autopilot message and every mode change, plus an altitude / mode / armed / mission item line every 15 s, until the drone has flown (above 3 m), landed and disarmed, or the timeout (1 hour) passes.
Listens for about 2 s and returns one line: flight mode, armed or not, GPS fix and satellites, altitude, battery percent and current mission item ('?' for anything not received).

Reads the options (--url, --timeout) and the subcommand, reads and checks the mission file when one is given (check-mission stops there with exit 0/1), connects a Vehicle and runs the chosen job: upload, wait-ready, arm, start, fly (upload + wait-ready + arm + start + confirm_takeoff), watch, status, mode, rtl, land or disarm.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: ros2 run sim_bringup mission_tool ... from demo.sh, fly_mission.sh, upload_mission.sh, status.sh, container_sim.sh and sim_demo run_reset.py

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: A small ROS 2 node 'odom_tf' that turns the drone's Gazebo odometry (/sim/drone/odometry, nav_msgs/Odometry, world ENU: x east, y north, z up) into TF frames so RViz can draw and follow the drone: one TF per message from the odometry frame to the drone frame ('world' -> 'base_link' for sim_models' iris_a8mini), plus one static identity TF from 'world' to the odometry frame when they differ.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: Started by sim.launch.py with the bridge (not for the stand-in drone). RViz's sim.rviz and sim_demo's markers both use the fixed frame 'world'.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: The ROS node class 'odom_tf': parameters odom_topic (/sim/drone/odometry), map_frame (world), odom_frame and base_frame ('' = take them from the message); it subscribes to the odometry with sensor QoS, broadcasts TF, and warns every 15 s while nothing arrives.
Creates the node 'odom_tf', declares its four parameters, makes a TF broadcaster and a static TF broadcaster, subscribes to the odometry topic and starts a 15 s timer for check_alive.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.effects: subscribes /sim/drone/odometry; logs which topic it uses

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: For each odometry message it publishes a TF from the odometry frame (default the message's frame, e.g. 'world') to the drone frame (e.g. 'base_link') with the message's position and orientation, stamped with the node's own clock (team nodes and RViz run on wall time). The first time it sees an odometry frame that is not the fixed frame, it also sends a static identity TF 'world' -> that frame.
Every 15 s, while no odometry has arrived yet, logs a warning asking whether the bridge runs and the drone is spawned.
Starts ROS, creates the OdomTf node and spins it until Ctrl+C, then shuts down cleanly.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: ros2 run sim_bringup odom_tf (sim.launch.py starts it as node 'odom_tf')

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: Tells the person running the demo, in plain words, what the drone is doing. A ROS node 'phase_monitor' listens to MAVROS and team-node topics (/mavros/state, /mavros/extended_state, /mavros/global_position/rel_alt, /mavros/statustext/recv and /send, /image_detection) and counts the photos in the team photo folder; a pure-Python state machine (MissionState) turns that into phases WAITING, ARMED, TAKEOFF, SEARCH, HOLD, TARGETS, DROP, RTL, LANDED. It prints one line per phase, every detection, a photo counter, a status line every 20 s, and a summary; it exits 0 when the drone has landed and disarmed.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: demo.sh and container_sim.sh run it in the background with --log <run>/phases.jsonl and wait for it to exit: that is how they know the flight is over. It parses the team's STATUSTEXT sentences, so those texts must not change (AGENTS.md rule).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.effects: prints to the terminal; appends JSON lines to the --log file

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: One thing worth printing: kind ('phase', 'detection', 'photo', 'info' or 'warn'), its text, and for a phase event the phase name.

The mission state machine, plain Python so it is unit-tested without ROS. It remembers phase, armed, mode, airborne, altitude, landed state, photo count, detections per class, drops and the targets text; each on_* method takes one piece of information and returns the Events to print.

Moves to a new phase and returns its 'phase' event with the phase's sentence (plus an optional detail in brackets). It never goes backwards, except from DROP back to TARGETS (flying on to the next target); repeating the same phase returns nothing.

Handles /mavros/state (about 1 Hz): reports mode changes, starts the RTL phase when the mode becomes RTL, settles a pending 'mission RTL item' (it counts only if the drone is still in AUTO 3 s later; a switch to GUIDED means main_controller took over to hold), starts ARMED when the drone arms, notes a disarm, and checks for landing.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: armed flag, mode name, optional time

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Handles the height above home (/mavros/global_position/rel_alt): the first time the armed drone is above 3 m it marks it airborne and starts TAKEOFF; it also checks for landing.
Handles MAVROS' landed_state from /mavros/extended_state (1 on ground, 2 in air, 3 taking off, 4 landing); 2 marks the flight as airborne. Then checks for landing.
Declares the flight finished (phase LANDED, once) when the drone has flown, is disarmed and is on the ground (landed_state 1 or below 1.5 m).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: list with the LANDED event or empty

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Handles ArduPilot's own messages (/mavros/statustext/recv). 'Mission: N Takeoff' starts TAKEOFF, 'Mission: N DigiCamCtrl' starts SEARCH, WP lines are noted while searching, and an 'RTL' item is only remembered (on_state decides later, because main_controller usually switches to GUIDED at that moment). PreArm/Arm texts become warnings; texts about disarming, landing, crash, failsafe or EKF are passed on.

Handles what the team's nodes send to the ground station (/mavros/statustext/send): 'Camera trigger STARTED' -> SEARCH, 'Reached last WP' / 'Holding to finish' -> HOLD, 'Targets: ...' -> TARGETS, 'Over ...' -> DROP, 'Servo C -> PWM' with PWM >= 1200 -> a PAYLOAD RELEASED line (channel 11 person, 13 tent), 'RTL' -> RTL. 'Detected ...', 'No valid targets', processing and FAILED/WARN texts become info or warning lines.

Handles one /image_detection result: stores each (class, score) and returns one line per detected person or tent with its confidence in percent, the photo's latitude/longitude ('NO GPS (0, 0)' when both are 0) and the photo name.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: photo name, list of (class, score), lat, lon

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Takes the number of photos in the team photo folder and prints a line for the first photo and then for every 10th one.
Returns the closing lines: flight time in minutes and last phase, number of photos, detections per class with the best confidence, the targets text and the payloads released.
Counts the finished photos (.jpg, .jpeg, .png) in a folder, ignoring the temporary '.tmp.' files video_cam writes before renaming; 0 if the folder cannot be read.

Runs the monitor: reads --log, --photo-dir, --timeout and --no-exit, creates the ROS node 'phase_monitor', subscribes to /mavros/state, /mavros/extended_state, /mavros/global_position/rel_alt, /mavros/statustext/recv, /mavros/statustext/send and (if the team's interfaces package is built) /image_detection, counts photos every 2 s, prints a status line, and watches that main_controller is still running. It spins until LANDED (exit 0), the timeout (exit 3) or Ctrl+C (130), then prints and logs the summary.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.effects: prints lines; appends to the JSON-lines log

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Prints each Event with a clock time ('===== PHASE n/8: NAME =====' for phases, 'DETECTION', '(!)' for warnings), appends it to the log file as a JSON line, and sets exit code 0 when the LANDED phase arrives (unless --no-exit).

Callback for /image_detection (interfaces/msg/ImageResult): collects every hypothesis with class_id '0' (person) or '1' (tent) and its score, then passes them with the photo name and latitude/longitude to MissionState.on_detection.
Every 5 s timer: when at least 20 s passed since the last one and the mission is under way, prints a status line with phase, mode, altitude, photo count and number of detections.

Every 5 s timer: looks at the running ROS node names; once main_controller has been seen and then disappears, it prints one loud warning that the team code crashed, so the audience is not waiting for drops that will never come.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: Takes one photo with the simulated camera. The team way (default) publishes true on /camera/trigger so the team's video_cam takes and downloads the photo into its photo folder ('<lat> , <lon>.jpg'); the direct way (--direct, or automatically when nobody listens) sends the SIYI SDK take-photo packet 55 66 01 01 00 00 00 0c 00 34 ce to the emulator at UDP 192.168.144.25:37260 and downloads the new file from its media web server on port 82 into ~/.astra_sim/photos. Exit 0 = new photo (path printed), 1 = none in time.
