mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: simulation/scripts/take_photo.sh runs it; it is a test button for the camera chain (video_cam -> siyi_emulator -> Gazebo photo camera).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Builds one SIYI SDK frame: bytes 55 66, the 'need answer' flag, data length and sequence number (2 bytes each, little-endian), the command id, the data, then a CRC-16/XMODEM checksum of everything before it. With command 0x0C and one data byte 00 it gives exactly the team's take-photo bytes 55 66 01 01 00 00 00 0c 00 34 ce.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: command id, data bytes, sequence, need_ack

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Downloads a URL and reads it as JSON; any network or JSON problem gives None.

Asks the camera's media server the same way video_cam does: GET .../cgi-bin/media.cgi/api/v1/getdirectories?media_type=0 on port 82, then getmedialist for the LAST folder (start 0, count 9999). Returns the folder and its file list, or ('', []) when the server does not answer.

The direct way: remembers the files already on the emulated SD card, sends the take-photo SDK packet by UDP to <camera_ip>:37260, then every 0.5 s re-reads the media list until a new file appears, and downloads that file into the output folder.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: path of the saved photo or None
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.effects: sends a UDP SDK packet; HTTP download; writes a .jpg

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: The team way: creates the ROS node 'photo_trigger', waits up to 4 s for a subscriber on /camera/trigger (the team's siyi node); if there is none it returns (False, None). Otherwise it publishes std_msgs/Bool true once and waits for a new photo file to appear in the team photo folder.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: (somebody listened, new file path or None)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Returns the set of finished image file names (.jpg/.jpeg/.png, no '.tmp.') in the photo folder; an unreadable folder gives an empty set.

Reads --direct, --camera-ip (192.168.144.25), --timeout (30 s), --photo-dir and --out-dir. Without --direct it tries the team topic first; when nobody listens it switches to the direct way and saves into ~/.astra_sim/photos. Prints 'NEW PHOTO: <path>' and returns 0, or explains what to check and returns 1.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: The single place that answers every 'where is it / which port' question of the simulator, with plain Python (no ROS node), so it can be unit-tested. It knows the state folder ~/.astra_sim, the SITL ports (5760+10I, 9002+10I ...), the MAVProxy ports 14550/14552/14553, how to reach Mission Planner on Windows from WSL, the camera profiles (zr10 2560x1440, a8mini 3840x2160), how a world name becomes world file + home + spawn + mission + truth, where SITL, its parameter files, MAVProxy and the ArduPilot Gazebo plugin are, how to make the drone SDF with xacro, which Gazebo topics are bridged to ROS, and where the team's photo folder and detector weights are.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: Used by sim.launch.py, team_stack.launch.py, phase_monitor and photo_trigger, and by the shell scripts through its small command line (python3 -m sim_bringup.sim_paths world runway mission | photo-dir | model-path | sim-home | sitl-ports I).

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Turns a text switch into True or False: '1', 'true', 'yes' and 'on' (any capitals, spaces ignored) give True, anything else False. Launch arguments always arrive as text, so this is how the launch file reads gui:=true and the like.
Expands '~' (the home folder) and $VARIABLES in a path text; an empty text stays empty.

Returns the folder where the simulator writes everything at run time: $ASTRA_SIM_HOME if set, else ~/.astra_sim. Inside it live sitl_I<n>/ (SITL's saved parameters eeprom.bin and logs), generated/ (drone model, bridge list), runs/ (one folder per demo run), state/ and models/ (the detector weights yolo26m.pt).
Returns the working folder of SITL instance I: <sim home>/sitl_I<I>. ArduCopter keeps its saved parameters and mission (eeprom.bin) there between runs, and MAVProxy writes mav.tlog there.
Returns <sim home>/generated, the folder for files the launch makes at every start: the drone model.sdf, the stand-in world and the bridge YAML.

Gives the port numbers of ArduCopter SITL instance I (SITL's -I option adds 10 x I to each): serial0 TCP 5760+10I (MAVProxy connects here and SITL waits for it), serial1 5762+10I (spare, e.g. a second ground station such as Mission Planner by TCP), serial2 5763+10I (the team's MAVROS: demo.sh and start_sim.sh use FCU_URL=tcp://127.0.0.1:5763+10I, wired like the real Jetson on the Pixhawk's TELEM2), fdm UDP 9002+10I (the physics link to Gazebo's ArduPilotPlugin) and rc_in UDP 5501+10I (unused). A negative instance raises ValueError. (The function's own comment still calls serial2 free; the scripts use it for MAVROS.)
Returns True inside Windows' WSL2, recognised by the word 'microsoft' in /proc/version (tests can pass their own text).

Finds out how WSL2 connects Ubuntu to Windows: it runs 'wslinfo --networking-mode' (WSL 2.0+) and returns its answer such as 'nat' or 'mirrored'; without that tool it says 'mirrored' when the network interface loopback0 exists, else 'nat'. Outside WSL it returns ''.

Reads the kernel route table /proc/net/route and returns the IPv4 address of the default gateway (the route with destination 00000000 that is up and uses a gateway; lowest metric wins). In WSL2 NAT networking that gateway is the Windows host itself, which is where Mission Planner listens; the address changes after a Windows restart, so it is looked up at every start.

Splits 'HOST' or 'HOST:PORT' (for example '192.168.1.20:14550') into (host, port), using the default port when none is given. It raises ValueError with a plain message for an empty host, spaces, extra colons or a port outside 1-65535.

Decides the extra MAVProxy output for a ground station on WINDOWS (Mission Planner / QGroundControl), because in WSL2 NAT networking Windows cannot hear Ubuntu's 127.0.0.1 outputs. Off when windows_gcs is false; an explicit windows_gcs_addr is used as given; otherwise WSL NAT gives udp:<default gateway>:14550, WSL mirrored gives udp:127.0.0.1:14551 (14550 is already the scripts' port there), and outside WSL nothing. It never doubles one of MAVProxy's own local ports.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py's add_mavproxy at every start
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: enabled switch, optional address, MAVProxy's local ports, optional mode/gateway for tests
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: ('udp:HOST:PORT' or '', list of plain-words notes for the log)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: A small data record with everything the launch needs about one world: name, world_file (.sdf path), home (SITL --home text 'lat,lon,alt_msl,heading', default the CMAC test field), spawn pose {x, y, z, yaw}, mission file, truth file, config_file, worlds_dir (its models/ and worlds/ go on Gazebo's resource path), standin flag and notes (remarks printed by the launch).
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.how_it_fits: Made by load_world_config / standin_world_config and read by sim.launch.py; not the same class as sim_worlds.world_config.WorldConfig.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Checks a SITL home text 'lat,lon,alt_msl,heading' and turns it into four numbers. It raises ValueError in plain words when there are not exactly 4 numbers, something is not a number, or latitude/longitude are out of range.
Builds a SITL home text from numbers: latitude and longitude with 7 decimals, altitude with 2, then the heading (the reverse of parse_home).

Finds the <spherical_coordinates> block of a world SDF text and reads latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation and heading_deg (a missing tag counts as 0). Returns None when the world has no such block. This lets a custom world give SITL a --home that matches the Gazebo picture.
Returns the name in the first <world name="..."> of an SDF text (for example 'astra_runway'), or 'default' when there is none. The stand-in bridge topics and the GUI need that name.

Turns the 'spawn' section of a world YAML into {x, y, z, yaw} with yaw in radians; it accepts 'yaw' (radians) or 'yaw_deg' (degrees). Missing keys keep the defaults x 0, y 0, z 0.2, yaw 0, and a section that is not a mapping adds a note and spawns at the origin.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: the raw YAML value, notes list

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Finds a file named in a world YAML: an absolute path is kept if it exists; a relative one is tried against each root folder in turn. Returns '' when nothing is found.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: path text, list of root folders

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Turns the launch argument world:= into a WorldConfig. A path to an .sdf is used directly (home from its <spherical_coordinates>, no mission or truth); a name like 'runway' reads sim_worlds/config/runway.yaml from the installed share (a .yaml path is read from its own folder) and resolves world_file, home, spawn, mission and truth. It never raises for a missing file: every problem goes into .notes so the launch prints it.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py and by the command line 'python3 -m sim_bringup.sim_paths world NAME FIELD' that demo.sh, fly_mission.sh and upload_mission.sh use
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: world text, sim_worlds share folder (or None)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Makes the world used when sim_worlds is not built: a copy of ardupilot_gazebo's iris_runway.sdf with its built-in iris_with_gimbal drone removed (the launch spawns its own 'iris'), saved as generated/standin_iris_runway.sdf. Home is the CMAC test field (-35.363262,149.165237,584,0), spawn z 0.195 m, yaw pi/2. It has no targets and no mission.
Goes through a list of candidate paths (with ~ and $VARS expanded) and returns the first that exists, and is runnable when want_exec is set. Returns None if none fits.
Finds the ArduCopter SITL program: the explicit path (sitl_bin:=), then $ARDUPILOT_SITL_BIN, ~/sitl/arducopter (made by 02_setup_ardupilot.sh) and /opt/ardupilot/build/sitl/bin/arducopter (Docker).
Finds one of ArduPilot's default parameter files, such as copter.parm or gazebo-iris.parm, in $ARDUPILOT_DEFAULT_PARAMS, ~/sitl or /opt/ardupilot/Tools/autotest/default_params.

Builds SITL's --defaults list in the contract order copter.parm, gazebo-iris.parm, then sim_models' astra_sitl.parm (ArduPilot reads them left to right, so later files win). Any missing file becomes a note, for example that payload servos 11/13 are not set up without astra_sitl.parm.

Finds the ArduPilot Gazebo plugin folder ($ARDUPILOT_GAZEBO_DIR, ~/ardupilot_gazebo, /opt/ardupilot_gazebo). A folder only counts when build/libArduPilotPlugin.so exists, the plugin that links the Gazebo drone to SITL.
Finds MAVProxy: the explicit path (mavproxy_bin:=), $ASTRA_MAVPROXY, ~/sitl/venv/bin/mavproxy.py (native setup) and finally mavproxy.py on the PATH (Docker).
Rewrites every <fdm_port_in> number in an SDF text to the given port, because SITL instance I talks to the drone's ArduPilotPlugin on UDP 9002 + 10 x I.

Makes the xacro arguments for sim_models' model.sdf.xacro: the live video size 1280x720 at 25 fps and lens hfov 1.4137 rad, the photo size of the camera profile (zr10 2560x1440 or a8mini 3840x2160) and fdm_port_in 9002+10I. An unknown camera model raises ValueError.

Makes the output folder look like the model's source folder by creating symbolic links to everything except the model.sdf* files (meshes/, model.config ...), replacing stale links. The generated model.sdf written next to them can then still use its relative mesh paths.

Produces the drone model file to spawn. It prefers the model:= file, then sim_models' iris_a8mini/model.sdf.xacro run through xacro with the camera profile and SITL port, then the pre-generated model.sdf. The result goes to <generated>/iris_a8mini_<camera>_I<I>/model.sdf beside links to the model's other files, with the fdm port patched. If xacro fails it falls back to the plain model.sdf (default photo size) and says so.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: sim_models share, camera model, SITL instance, output root, optional explicit model

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Makes the drone used when sim_models is not built: ardupilot_gazebo's iris_with_gimbal (3-axis gimbal, 640x480 camera, no photo camera, no payloads) with its fdm port patched, copied to <generated>/standin_iris_with_gimbal_I<I>/.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: ardupilot_gazebo folder, SITL instance, output root

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Lists the topics ros_gz_bridge copies from Gazebo into ROS 2 (all one way, Gazebo to ROS): /sim/camera/video/image -> /sim/camera/image (live picture), /sim/camera/video/camera_info -> /sim/camera/camera_info, /sim/camera/photo/image -> /sim/camera/photo (each photo), /sim/drone/odometry (nav_msgs/Odometry) and /sim/gimbal/joint_states (sensor_msgs/JointState from gz.msgs.Model). Camera topics are 'lazy' (converted only while somebody watches). For the stand-in drone it maps ardupilot_gazebo's gimbal camera topic instead.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: standin flag, world name, entity name

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Builds one bridge entry dict with ros_topic_name, gz_topic_name, both message type names, direction GZ_TO_ROS and the lazy flag.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: Gazebo topic, ROS topic, ROS type, Gazebo type, lazy

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Writes the bridge entries as a YAML list (with a 'do not edit, rewritten at every launch' header) to the given file, normally ~/.astra_sim/generated/bridge_I<I>.yaml, and returns its path for parameter_bridge's config_file parameter.
Returns the Linux-side copy of the team repo: $ASTRA_REPO if set, else ~/ODLC_Machine_Inferencing_System_2025-2026 (the copy 03_build.sh makes).

Returns the folder where the team's video_cam saves photos and new_od reads them, following video_cam's own rule: walk up from where video_cam is installed to the folder holding both install/ and src/, then src/video_cam/mapping_photos. It does not import video_cam on purpose (that imports OpenCV, which breaks later Qt windows). An override wins; if the team stack is not built it falls back to the repo copy's ros2_ws/src/video_cam/mapping_photos.

Removes QT_QPA_PLATFORM_PLUGIN_PATH, QT_QPA_FONTDIR and QT_PLUGIN_PATH from the environment when they point into a Python package folder (site-packages / dist-packages), as OpenCV's pip wheel sets them. Otherwise Gazebo, RViz and the demo panel abort with 'Could not load the Qt platform plugin'. Returns the removed names.

Reads the gui_env launch argument 'NAME=value,NAME2=value2' into a dict of environment variables for the Gazebo window only (troubleshooting, e.g. QSG_RENDER_LOOP=basic so Qt draws the window on its main thread when the camera panel flickers). Spaces around items are ignored and a value may contain '=' but not ','; an item without '=' or with an invalid variable name is skipped and listed as a problem.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: by sim.launch.py when it starts the Gazebo window

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Returns the detector's folder of annotated images, detection_results_sahi, which sits next to the photo folder.

Returns the YOLO weights file for the team's real detector in the simulator: $ASTRA_DETECTOR_MODEL, else ~/.astra_sim/models/yolo26m.pt (downloaded by 03_build.sh). It is kept outside the repo so no Jetson-only .engine file sits next to it (new_od would try to load that first).

The small command line for shell scripts: 'world NAME FIELD' prints mission, truth, world_file, home, name, config or worlds_dir of a world; 'photo-dir', 'model-path', 'sim-home' and 'sitl-ports I' print those answers. Prints the answer and returns 0, or prints a usage line and returns 2 for a bad question.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: python3 -m sim_bringup.sim_paths ... (demo.sh, start_sim.sh, fly_mission.sh, upload_mission.sh, container_sim.sh)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: exit code; the answer on standard output

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: Waits until the team's flight stack (./launcher.sh sim) is ready to fly. Checked every second: MAVROS connected (/mavros/state), the six team nodes running (waypoint_manager, main_controller, siyi, mission_camera_trigger, new_od, gps_mavros_service_node), and waypoint_manager's parameter buffer_wp >= 0 (it has read the mission). Optional: --need-detector waits for new_od's /sahi/get_health 'ModelLoaded: True', --settle S checks the nodes are still alive S seconds later. Exit 0 ready, 1 not ready.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: demo.sh and container_sim.sh run it before arming, so the drone never takes off while the team code is still starting; it reads waypoint_manager's parameters at most once per second so it does not starve main_controller's own reads. --skip-node / --add-node adapt it to plug-in profiles, --no-mission to Mission Planner mode.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Turns new_od's health text such as 'Healthy: True, ConsecErrors: 0, ModelLoaded: True, Format: pytorch' into a dict (split at commas, then at the first colon).
Returns the wanted node names that are not running, comparing only the last part of each running name (namespaces and the leading '/' ignored).

Builds the list of nodes to wait for: the six TEAM_NODES minus the --skip-node names plus the --add-node names (used when a plug-in profile replaced a team node). With neither option it is exactly TEAM_NODES.

Creates the ROS node 'stack_check', subscribes to /mavros/state and makes clients for /waypoint_manager/get_parameters and /sahi/get_health. It loops (spin 0.5 s, poll the services, list what is missing, print every 10 s) until ready or --timeout (300 s); then optionally waits for the detector model (--detector-timeout 240 s, warning only) and does the --settle check.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: ros2 run sim_bringup stack_check --timeout 600 --settle 20 ... (demo.sh; container_sim.sh; START OVER)

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: If a service request has waited more than 3 s without an answer (answers can get lost while the team stack starts), it removes that request from the client and forgets it, so a new one can be sent.

Sends at most one GetParameters request per second for buffer_wp and rtl_index to waypoint_manager and at most one /sahi/get_health request per second, and stores the answers (buffer_wp as an integer, the health text parsed with parse_health). It never blocks: it only checks whether earlier requests are done.

Lists what is not ready yet: 'MAVROS connection to the autopilot', each missing 'node <name>', and (unless --no-mission) 'waypoint_manager mission indices (buffer_wp)' while buffer_wp is unknown or negative.
Prints a line with the prefix '[stack_check] ' and flushes it.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.explain: A helper that waits until a network port is open (or a file exists) and then turns itself into the given program. It keeps the start order Gazebo -> SITL -> MAVProxy: SITL may only start once the drone's ArduPilotPlugin has bound UDP 9002+10I, and MAVProxy only once SITL listens on TCP 5760+10I. It checks the kernel's socket tables in /proc/net instead of connecting, because a test connection to 5760 would count as SITL's first client.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/s.how_it_fits: sim.launch.py starts SITL and MAVProxy through it ('wait_then_exec --udp-port 9002 -- arducopter ...'); START OVER (sim_demo run_reset.py) recognises and unwraps these commands. Exit codes: never returns on success, 1 timeout, 2 bad usage.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Reads one kernel socket table (/proc/net/tcp, udp, tcp6 or udp6), skips the header line and collects the local port of every line (the hex number after the last ':' of the local address). For TCP only sockets in state 0A (LISTEN) count; for UDP every bound socket counts.

Returns every local port that is bound (UDP) or listening (TCP) on this computer, IPv4 and IPv6 together, by reading /proc/net/<proto> and /proc/net/<proto>6. A missing IPv6 table is fine. sim.launch.py also uses it to refuse a start when SITL's ports are already in use.
Lists in words what is not ready yet, such as 'UDP port 9002', 'TCP port 5760' or 'file /path'. An empty list means everything is ready.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.inputs: UDP ports, TCP ports, files to wait for

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.explain: Reads its own options before '--' (--udp-port, --tcp-port, --file, --timeout default 180 s, --delay, --label) and the program after it. Every 0.2 s it checks missing_conditions, printing what it waits for every 10 s; on timeout it prints 'GAVE UP' and returns 1. When everything is ready it waits the extra delay and replaces itself with the program (os.execvp), so Ctrl+C from the launch reaches the program directly.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.called_when: ros2 run sim_bringup wait_then_exec ... (sim.launch.py: SITL with --timeout 420, MAVProxy with --timeout 480 --delay 1)
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.outputs: exit code 1 or 2 on failure; on success the process becomes the program
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/si.effects: starts the given program in its own place

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.explain: A developer tool (not a test): it builds the same named dock panes as rviz/sim.rviz in an invisible PyQt5 window, arranges them (Displays left, 3D view middle, big camera POV above the newest photo on the right) and writes Qt's saved-layout blob into the .rviz file.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.how_it_fits: Run by hand after changing the RViz layout: QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 test/gen_rviz_window_state.py --write rviz/sim.rviz.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.explain: One command for every quick check of sim_bringup and the simulator scripts: the pytest unit tests, both launch files parsed with --show-args, bash -n and shellcheck on simulation/setup/*.sh and simulation/scripts/*.sh, and every script's --help. It never starts Gazebo or SITL. Exit 0 all passed, 1 something failed.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.how_it_fits: Test runner for teammates after changing sim_bringup or simulation/scripts (needs 03_build.sh first; it sources sim_env.sh).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.explain: Unit tests for mission_tool's mission-file reader without an autopilot: QGC WPL 110 parsing, the checks against what the team code expects (TAKEOFF, DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL, two survey waypoints after it, RETURN_TO_LAUNCH last) and the 1e7 scaling of MISSION_ITEM_INT coordinates.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_bringup (no ROS needed).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.explain: Unit tests for the phase monitor's state machine: a whole mission is replayed as the texts and numbers MAVROS and the team nodes publish, and the phases, detections, drops and the 'landed' end are checked.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_bringup (no ROS needed).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.explain: Unit tests for sim_paths: world configs, homes, spawn poses, ports, the Windows ground-station output, the gui_env parser, the drone SDF generation and the stand-ins, all with fake share folders made in a temporary directory (no ROS, no Gazebo).

Unit tests for the small helpers: photo_trigger's SIYI packet builder must give exactly the bytes video_cam sends, stack_check's health parser and node check, and sim.launch.py's argument list (every contract argument exists, plus the Windows ground station switch and the gui_env switch, empty by default).
Unit tests for wait_then_exec with fake /proc/net tables (UDP 9002 bound, TCP 5760 listening) and one real subprocess run where the helper replaces itself with 'echo'.

fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.explain: Inner helper of _launch_setup: returns the installed path of one of sim_bringup's Gazebo window layouts (config/gazebo_gui.config, gazebo_gui_no_camera.config or gazebo_camera_window.config), or '' when that file is not installed. With the ardupilot_gazebo stand-in drone, whose camera publishes on another topic, it first writes a copy <name>_standin.config into ~/.astra_sim/generated/ with /sim/camera/video/image replaced by the stand-in's camera topic, and returns that copy.
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.called_when: when the Gazebo window starts with one of our layouts (gui:=true), and once more for the camera window with gui_camera:=window
fn:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/la.outputs: path of the layout file, or ''

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/c.explain: The layout of a small extra Gazebo window (700 x 460, dark theme) that shows ONLY the drone's live gimbal camera: one ImageDisplay panel 'Drone camera (live)' on the Gazebo topic /sim/camera/video/image, with the topic picker switched off and no 3D view.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/c.how_it_fits: sim.launch.py opens it as a second 'gz sim -g' window (process gz_camera_window) when gui_camera:=window, next to a main window without a camera panel (gazebo_gui_no_camera.config). Why: on the team laptop (WSL2, Mesa D3D12) the camera panel inside the main window sometimes shows old pictures of the 3D view; a window with no 3D view cannot mix them up (docs/simulation/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/c.explain: The main Gazebo window layout WITHOUT the live camera panel: gazebo_gui.config with the 'Camera POV (live)' ImageDisplay taken out. It keeps the big 3D view (MinimalScene), the scene manager, mouse view control, CameraTracking (the /gui/follow service gz_follow uses), markers, entity selection and right-click menu, and the play/pause and real-time-factor boxes (1500 x 900, dark theme).
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/c.how_it_fits: sim.launch.py uses it for the main window with gui_camera:=window (the camera then has its own window, gazebo_camera_window.config) and gui_camera:=off (no camera picture in Gazebo; RViz and Mission Planner still show it). test_gui_configs.py checks that only the camera panel differs from gazebo_gui.config.

mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.explain: Checks the Gazebo window layouts in config/ without starting Gazebo: every layout file is readable XML, the camera-only window (gui_camera:=window) holds exactly one camera panel that listens to /sim/camera/video/image, and gazebo_gui_no_camera.config is gazebo_gui.config with ONLY the camera panel taken out, so the two files cannot drift apart unnoticed.
mod:ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_bringup/t.how_it_fits: pytest suite of sim_bringup (no ROS, no Gazebo).
